RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Resuming (32-weeks). Ex Michael Grantham in WA. Took his game to another level winning the Northerly Stakes last prep. Excellent first up record. Soft jump-out here 1/7. Leading contender.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: N S Psaltis, Mrs G C Psaltis Et Al
Spotlight: Great run at Flemington 20 Jun. Put in some good work late this course. Very fit and not out of this.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: Bennett Racing Pty Ltd (N Bennett), D Hardie Et Al
Spotlight: Let-up (49-days). Sent out $13 when unable to threaten at Eagle Farm when second-up. Sharper now and can make his presence felt with even breaks.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: A T Biacsi, D Angely Et Al
Spotlight: First-up (23-weeks). Ex S V Vahala in Victoria. Last win was 23 Nov 2024. 1st & 4th at recent jump-outs. Place claims preferred.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Raced in back half and was never in a position to mount a serious challenge this track. Needs to recapture form.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: A J Hehir, D W Rasheed Et Al
Spotlight: Knuckled down with purpose in choppy conditions here last time. Key player.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: R A Holburt, B R Holburt Et Al
Spotlight: Annexed the (Bm84) at Caulfield 27 Jun. Rallied powerfully from midfield to salute this venue. See no reason he can't bring up a hat-trick of wins.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: D J Oliphant, P J Salter Et Al
Spotlight: Went back, closed intently this track off long break. Will be better for the outing. Must be considered.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: D M D B Syndicate, Grahame Begg Racing Et Al
Spotlight: Midfield and worked home solidly in rain affected going at Flemington second-up. Others with greater appeal.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 260,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Naval Crown; no show, however, when 25-1 for maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month, behind Public Affection.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 55,000gns yearling by Dark Angel; second foal; dam US 5f-8.5f turf winner, out of graded-placed US 1m winner; gelded and others look more striking on paper, even though stable was off the mark with this year's 2yos this month.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: Seventh foal; Havana Grey half-brother to winners Mister Winston (7.6f-8.5f; RPR 106), Kinks (5f-7f including 2yo/Bahrain; 96) and Crazee Icon (7.6f; 84); dam 6f AW winner (70), closely related to Listed-placed 5f winner Thesme; late foal but with in-form trainer who won this race in 2022 and 2023, both with something second time out.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 135,000gns yearling by Siyouni; third foal; half-brother to 10.6f AW winner Seola (RPR 70); dam French 7.5f 2yo/10.5f Listed winner, closely related to useful French 7f winner Markhor, out of 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Vorda; from a leading stable, so needs a close look.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: By No Nay Never out of 5f/5.7f winner (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 108); 15-2 when second of 11 for novice at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 26 days ago, running on from midfield; that form has taken some knocks but still makes appeal in this line-up and this Group 2 Gimcrack entry showed plenty of promise.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 75,000euros yearling, 280,000euros breeze-up 2yo by Perfect Power; third foal; dam unplaced at 7.5f-10.5f in France, sister to US 1m Grade 2 winner Tamahere, half-sister to 10.5f Listed winner Shadan; leading yard has not yet found its stride with 2yos this term but he still needs a check.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 110,000euros yearling by Showcasing; 10-1 when sixth of 13 in maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 33 days ago, making some of the running; showed ability but big improvement is needed.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 3,000gns yearling by Sergei Prokofiev; ran a great deal better than 150-1 suggested he would in a novice at Newbury (6f, good to firm) 16 days ago, getting hampered at the start but running on into sixth of 18, beaten just over 2l; it's not the best form in this field but was a promising debut.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 180,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Havana Grey; 11-1 when beaten a shade over 3l in a novice at Nottingham (6f, good) early last month, coming from towards rear for fourth of 12; non-runner twice since; looks sure to improve and has major each-way claims for in-form stable.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Returned to form when fourth in first-time visor at Ripon (5f, good) three weeks ago despite stumbling and nearly losing his rider at the start; possibilities off same mark if the headgear has the same effect.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Probably best at 5f and went down by only a head at Pontefract five weeks ago; had previously shaped well when fifth in a big field on this course; trainer has won this race three times in the last eight seasons and Johnny Burke looks a positive jockey booking.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Front-runner who was beaten off only inside the final 1f at Lingfield last time; should make another bold bid but he's still 4lb higher than when making all at Yarmouth in the spring.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Tough cookie who arrives in peak form after a close third over C&D two weeks ago; one of three with serious claims for her local yard.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: 4lb lower than for his last two 6f wins but recent efforts have been underwhelming and he's unproven over the minimum trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Hard to fancy on recent efforts with no better than a tenth-placed finish in his last five starts; however, he could be revived by a recent stable switch (from Seb Spencer) and he's fully 18lb lower than when eighth in the 5f handicap at Royal Ascot last summer; worth monitoring in the market.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Prominent racer; on a lenient mark but his losing sequence is mounting and he had no obvious excuses when beating just one home at Beverley three weeks ago.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Had slipped in the weights before returning to form when second of 12 at Newcastle last month, coming close to landing a gamble; still 4lb below his last winning mark and should be in the mix again.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: C&D winner earlier in career and also won off today's mark at Ripon in May, but he's been tailed off on his last two outings and urgently needs a reversal of fortune.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Has had far less racing than most of these and showed he retains ability when fifth of eight at Beverley (5f, good to firm; 11-1) three weeks ago after a long absence, a gelding operation and a stable switch; big player if coming on for that run and Danny McMenamin was the successful rider in this race last year, for the same connections.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: In good form in the spring, winning over this trip at Southwell, but his two most recent runs have been some way below par; others preferred.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
OwnerName: Ingleby Bloodstock Ltd & The Ivy League
Spotlight: June win came in a small field at Catterick (5f) but he finished behind Kodiac Thriller when only seventh of nine at Ripon next time; well beaten on only run at York; bit to prove.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Seems to be going through the motions and his losing run stretches back over two years; needs to stop the slide but he's on a dangerous mark if staging a revival, so impossible to rule out.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: 3-11 on turf; steadily progressive but most recent success came off 11lb lower and she'll need another personal best to notch win number four.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Two 5f wins in 2026 and he ran respectably when third at Hamilton two weeks ago; prone to the odd poor run, however, and others are higher up the list.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Winning for the fourth time when scoring at Beverley in June, and he was narrowly beaten in a blanket finish there on Monday; not ruled out.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Plucky veteran who retains plenty of vim and vigour, another fine run when second in amateurs' race at Doncaster last time; 3lb out of the weights but has finished third in the last two runnings of this event and has each-way possibilities once more.
Latest of his nine wins was over C&D in February off a 1lb higher mark; that helps show that he needs a second look, despite mixed fortunes since.

Eight AW wins, including under Conor Whiteley at Wolverhampton (1m6f) in May and Newcastle (1m4f) in June; failed to prove her effectiveness on turf on latest start and the trip this short is a concern, but she has to be respected back on AW.
AW regular who scored here (1m2f) in December and has strung together a long line of minor honours this year; should be seriously involved.

1m turf and 1m2f AW winner for the Crisfords but he never took off for Mike Smith and finished last of seven on his stable debut ten weeks ago; impossible to recommend without a market move to offer revival hopes.

Ex-Irish; 0-12 overall and, after nearly a year off, well beaten on both starts for new stable (22-1 and 28-1); the positives are that she's down the weights and steps back up from 1m1f/1m for this AW debut.

Most of her best AW efforts were on Polytrack but there was a 2024 second on Wolverhampton Tapeta; won at Thirsk (1m4f) on this day last year off a 3lb higher mark; no joy since but her Ayr fourth (1m2f) on latest start was a healthy step back in the right direction.

Two C&D runs (fourth on first occasion) last autumn are the sum of her AW racing experience; 3-14 on turf thanks to winning three times over 1m2f under Jake Dickson in the space of four starts last August/September; big shout on peak form, which she's not quite reproduced this season.

0-10; sold out of the Greenall/Guerriero yard for 4,000gns in June; five-runner race at Nottingham (1m2f) eight days ago on stable debut was the third time he's finished second and another was on Wolverhampton Tapeta last December; place possibility.
Veteran who is 12-110 overall and 4-26 on Newcastle AW; his last two wins were on turf last autumn; 2026 form has not been great but the return to this track (first time this year) might offer hope.

Runner-up three times in a row over 1m3f/1m4f on turf this summer and her 1m2f fourth at Ayr was similar form; big shout on that but the problem is that her AW form (six races, including three last autumn) is at a lower level.

OwnerName: R Whitelock, L Clemitson & R Jefferson
Spotlight: Had a hurdles win in spring 2025 and 2026; ten-race maiden on Flat but placed in four of his five attempts this year, including three times over C&D; had wind surgery after latest but firmly in the mix if all is okay.

Three wins from his first four Flat starts in 2026, including one over C&D; that record demands respect but he pulled up 25 days ago (bled from the nose) and needs to bounce back from that; 7lb claimer takes over.
17-race maiden who came last in both starts this summer, one C&D; bits of form last year and cheekpieces (worn on last seven starts) are removed.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E55,000 yearling; eighth foal; half-sister by Churchill to five winners, best of them Sixteen Arches (American Grade 2-placed); dam unraced half-sister to 5f 2yo Group 3 winner Tournedos;

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E40,000 yearling; third foal; half-sister by Dandy Man to two winners; dam German Listed-placed 6f winner, half-sister to a German 1m1f Listed winner.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Not a bad run at a huge price on debut at the Curragh; also some merit in last week's Leopardstown run; not a likely maiden winner, but could be interesting in a nursery after this.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E42,000 yearling; State Of Rest filly is a half-sister to 6f AW 2yo winner Karaoke; dam US 6.5f dirt winner, half-sister to Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf winner Hootenanny; stable set to have best season, but yet to have a juvenile winner this term.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Showed the benefit of two Roscommon outings when producing an improved display in a 7f maiden at Down Royal eight days ago; finished in front of a shorter-priced stablemate in chasing home the front-running favourite (trained by Aidan O'Brien); cheekpieces may help; sets a fair standard.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E15,000 yearling, first foal; dam AW winner, sister to 2yo Group 3 winner/1m Group 1-placed Marie's Diamond, half-sister to Australian 1m2f Listed winner Sikandarabad.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E20,000 yearling; fifth foal; half-sister to winners in the US and Slovakia; dam unraced half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Strathspey.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E20,000 yearling; Harry Angel filly, first foal; dam German 1m1f winner, half-sister to winners Vif Monsieur (German Group 3), Vive Ma Fille (Listed-placed 1m4f) and Vision Clear (1m4f Flat/2m hurdle).

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister by State Of Rest to five winners, best of them a 7f Listed scorer; not beaten far in a decent maiden at the Curragh last Sunday; could run into the money now with that experience under her belt.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Never in the hunt first time out at Leopardstown; stable's second-string then, same scenario now.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E8,000 yearling; sixth foal; half-sister to a bumper winner; useful winning dam, half-sister by Holy Roman Emperor to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Stonemason, out of sister to Jersey Stakes winner River Deep; from a recently-established local stable.

240,000gns breeze-up buy who won easily on debut at Lingfield (5f, good to firm) in May and kept on well for sixth of 27 in the Group 2 Queen Mary here at the Royal meeting (5f, good to firm); the step up to 6f could be a positive move and she's a leading contender.

Impressive on debut at Goodwood (6f, good) in May and confirmed that promise when fourth of 25 in the Group 3 Albany Stakes over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm); she has to be firmly in calculations.

16-1 winner for Michael Keady on debut at Thirsk (5f, good) in May, despite being denied a clear run, and then sixth of 25 at 80-1 in the Group 3 Albany over C&D (good to firm); she has just over 3l to find with Dark Issue (who was fourth) on that Royal Ascot form but could have more to offer; sold for £150,000 just before the Royal meeting; respected on stable debut.

Made all on debut at Windsor (6f, good to soft) last month then dead-heated for first in a Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good to firm), where she was the 7-4 favourite; open to further improvement and represents last year's winning yard; she's one to consider.

Improved upon her first two runs when 1l third of 25 at 125-1 in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm; Moonrise second); can be in the mix if backing up that performance.
Won modest novice race at Kempton (6f, AW) in May on second run, then well beaten at 300-1 in the Albany over C&D (good to firm); hard to fancy.

95,000euros yearling; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Arcano; 6-1, won by 7l in six-runner novice on last month's debut at Chepstow (6f, good to soft); this is a vastly tougher race but she's clearly a bright prospect; remains to be seen where her limitations lie.

Made all at 5-1 in small-field novice at Kempton (6f, AW) on debut then went close at 66-1 in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes here (6f, good to firm) at the Royal meeting, racing prominently throughout; on the shortlist.
280,000gns yearling who won at 12-1 on this month's debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm); others have more substance to their form but she's a likeable prospect who has plenty of scope to progress.

Won at Ripon (6f, good) in May on second start and suited by the return to 6f when close Listed third at Newmarket last month (good to firm; led; behind Glorious Game); stable won this in 2017 and 2023 but she needs another step forward if she's to come out on top today.

OwnerName: Gary Matthews, Steve Weston & Lucky Hat
Spotlight: Made it 2-2 with easy win in four-runner Listed race at the Curragh (5f, good) in May; faded in Group 3 at Naas (6f, good) next time but kept on well when eighth of 27 in the Group 2 Queen Mary here (5f, good to firm) at the Royal meeting, where she didn't enjoy an ideal passage; closely matched with Alta Regina on that latest form and the return to 6f is worth a go; chance.
Novice win in 2024 remains his sole win in 18 Flat races and he has performed poorly in his two previous visits here; well-held third over hurdles last week; not overly appealing.

1m2f/1m3f wins on the AW; showed little in two runs over hurdles before returning from a break and wind surgery with a fourth of ten at Southwell in January; now back from another break, others are safer.
This year's four wins have been in Class 6s but it was very clearcut at Beverley (1m4f, good to form) three weeks ago when the cheekpieces were back on; he's still fairly treated off 4lb higher.

Multiple winner who took advantage of her much reduced mark when justifying favouritism at Bath (extended 1m3f, firm); entitled to go well again off 4lb higher; ran okay in one or her two previous visits here.

Front-running tactics in the new blinkers didn't work two runs ago but he had cover before coming home 7l clear at Leicester 11 days ago (1m4f, good to firm); up 7lb but clear claims should he deliver something similar.
Victory in this two years ago is one of two course wins; dangerously treated if revived by a return to this venue and he did win on the AW in May.

No wins in seven but still went off odds-on for his second crack at a handicap last time at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) where a slow start did him no favours in a steadily run race; that wasn't the first time he's been slowly away so that's a concern around here, but the ability is there.
Only had seven races and two since gelded; first try over as far as 1m3f when nosed out at Hamilton (good) two weeks ago; considered.

Left Ralph Beckett for 24,000gns and as a seven-race maiden; does have competitive form off this mark, including last time when tried in cheekpieces (had worn blinkers in two previous races); hard to discount.
Tailed off in a maiden here last year; respectable efforts over 1m4f at Wolverhampton last month but looks better on the AW and he does have his quirks.

Rated 5lb higher than when a close fifth in this race 12 months ago; has done well on AW since, winning at Southwell (well backed) on New Year's Day and finishing a good fourth at Newcastle four weeks ago; not obviously thrown in but could still have a bit more to come.

Just one win to his name since returning to action in November and that is scant reward for some fine efforts, including an unlucky defeat over 5f here in May; good third at Chester (6f, good; drawn wide) four weeks ago; remains a sprinter of interest.

Began the year with two good efforts at Newbury and Newmarket; beaten favourite on his last two starts but that is not to say this mark will prove beyond him if things pan out more favourably; each-way shout if a high draw doesn't prove to be a negative.

Admirable campaigner down the years and although he hasn't placed in three visits to York, he has been poorly drawn in two of them and ran well in Listed company on the other occasion; looked to retain ability when third at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) on 2000 Guineas day and he shouldn't be crabbed for his Wokingham effort as he trounced the only other rival to race up the stands' rail; it has been a long time since he's had a mark this low; big run on the cards.

OwnerName: Doug Graham, Ian Davison, Alan Drysdale
Spotlight: Veteran who ran a cracker behind a stablemate over C&D at last season's Ebor meeting; runner-up twice in Bahrain in January; low-key return to Britain last week; on a good mark but this is a tough race in which to try and rebound.
Made good progress in the second half of 2025; the handicapper has held the upper hand more recently though and this might not set up ideally for his style of racing.

5f win on this card last year and he followed it was a hugely eye-catching third over 5.4f at the Ebor meeting; back in the winners' enclosure at Beverley in April and he has run well in defeat here and at Newcastle on his last two starts; can fluff the start and he still has to prove himself at 6f but there is an air of unfinished business surrounding him.
Made a winning stable debut at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) in April; two good 6f runs this month too but he will need to pull out more if he is to come out on top this afternoon.

Progressive sprinter in 2025 (following wind surgery) and he has carried on the good work this year, winning 6f handicaps at Doncaster in May (good to soft) and June (good to firm); well beaten at Thirsk 24 days ago, however, and this is a deeper race.
The winner of two of his three starts in 2026, notably a big-field Class 4 over C&D six weeks ago; 4lb higher in a stronger race and his draw may not be advantageous.

His form has taken off since dropped to 6f, winning at Ripon and Hamilton in May and posting fine efforts in defeat over C&D and at Newmarket since; no obvious reason why he wouldn't be in the shake up again.

Three poor runs to begin his turf campaign but he underwent wind surgery in June and returned to form with a close second at Chester (6f, good) four weeks ago; not certain to confirm those placings with Stratusnine.

He has run well over C&D in the past and he arrives in fine form, winning 5f handicaps at Haydock and Carlisle (soft/good to soft) this summer; the 5lb rise is less of a concern than either his draw in stall 22 or the forecast faster ground.

Won a good C&D handicap last year and also successful at Ayr last September; 0-7 in 2026 but he retains all his ability and ran well for third (of 17) at Ayr 19 days ago; high draw a potential stumbling block.
Ended 2025 in fine form on AW; 0-7 in 2026 but he has slipped 6lb below his last winning mark and has Toby Moore taking another 7lb off his back; suspicion a few will prove stronger.

Won last season's Portland handicap at Doncaster off a 1lb higher mark; she made a slow start to 2026 but there have been encouraging signs more recently, fourth at Ayr (6f, soft) and then second at Doncaster (5f, good to firm); form dipped here (5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; could bounce back.

Beat 17 rivals at Thirsk in April and he has finished second three times since, including a big-field C&D handicap; missed out by a short-head at Newmarket last week; solid form claims despite small rise in the weights.

Promising at up to 1m for Ger Lyons as a 2yo; unplaced in his first two runs (7f/1m1f) for this yard but he turned in a career-best effort when second of 14 (behind a handicap blot; pair clear) over C&D four weeks ago; showed good speed on that occasion and he should make a bold bid from stall 1 despite a 4lb rise.

He is a better horse on AW than turf, last seen suffering miserable luck in running at Newcastle (6f) four weeks ago off a 17lb higher mark than today's; can win races on turf off this sort of mark but perhaps not this one.
Promising in his first three 2yo runs but he couldn't quite cut the mustard in nurseries thereafter; gelded prior to his reappearance; still has time to do better but he returns in a warm race.
Stayed on from well off the pace to take third in a 0-80 over C&D a fortnight ago; this is tougher but likely to give another good account.
Run of in-frame efforts came to an end here two weeks ago but he still ran with more promise than his finishing position suggests; still likely vulnerable at this level.

First run since leaving Noel Meade in Ireland for £70,000 in May; a pretty useful jumper for him (second on chase debut two weeks earlier) and won a 1m4f maiden in April 2025 in his latest Flat race; unexposed in this sphere (makes AW debut) and not written off.

Signed off for Ralph Beckett in good form on AW in autumn 2024 but, following a long absence, he was well held this summer in his two runs for new connections; some ability remains but he's best watched for now.
Very useful bumper performer and hurdler who won at Kempton (1m4f, Polytrack) 23 days ago on his Flat handicap debut, despite being first off the bridle; up 4lb but more to give in this sphere.

Eight starts, with sole win on handicap debut at Catterick (1m4f, soft) last October; fourth on all four outings since but at least the best of those was on AW (Lingfield Polytrack on penultimate start); hooded last two; others look a bit more solid.

8yo who has run 20 times at Newcastle (vastly more than any other track) and had two wins here plus six seconds; latest second was in the 2m Northumberland Vase on latest start, having also been placed at this track three times over 1m2f this year, so he is likely to serve up the same highly competitive show over today's 1m4f.

Won off 1lb lower at Southwell (1m4f, Tapeta) last November, from eight races; back near that form when second of five on turf at Chepstow (made most) three weeks ago, so enters calculations on this first run under a claiming rider.

Won once each in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 but has not scored since and this season he's not at all been the force of old; wore cheekpieces on last two outings, with a respectable show on first occasion; the last of his three AW races was in 2024; unpersuasive.

Placed at Nottingham, Newbury (1m2f) and Carlisle (1m1f) in his three races before this handicap/AW debut; it was admittedly a shock defeat at 1-4 when beaten a neck last time but that was against a once-race Juddmonte colt and probably still a creditable effort; this trip makes appeal and he's a very different sort to the older, more exposed runners in this; one to note.

Sole AW run (he came last) was in 2023; overall 3-15 in France and very well handicapped judged on plenty of 2025 form but he's not beaten many in his four runs for new stable; hard to latch on to unless there's been vastly more market interest in him this time.

0-6 for Donnacha O'Brien in Ireland but staying-on third of ten in a maiden at Leopardstown (1m5f, good to firm) last time was his best form; flopped in 1m2f handicap the time before and also modest in his only AW race, but a positive start for his new connections is by no means ruled out.

OwnerName: Mr & Mrs G F Hall Racing
Spotlight: The last two of his seven wins were at this track, albeit in 2024; placed twice over 1m2f here in a mixed campaign last autumn/winter; well beaten at 25-1 five weeks ago, a run which he may have needed after six months off and he's now back to his last winning mark, but this race looks too hot.

Minor form improvement on all starts, getting off the mark (fifth attempt) when 4-6 in a four-runner handicap at Hamilton (1m3f) on latest; carried her head a bit high that day but had to battle to lead on the line; up 3lb for this AW debut but she's a lightly raced 3yo who may still do better.

OwnerName: All For One Racing Ix & Chris Wright
Spotlight: Had wind and gelding operations before reappearance; 6-4 co-favourite for a seven-runner handicap at Goodwood (1m2f, soft) six weeks ago on second run back and improved to win from the front, asserting in clearcut fashion; up 6lb and needs another step forward but that may well be possible.
Godolphin cast-off; rated 74 after making the frame on all three starts for Charlie Appleby; now down to 60; very weak form in three handicap attempts.
Has looked very limited; 50-1 when finishing in rear over 1m at Bellewstown on handicap/seasonal debut at Bellewstown.

First four runs were at Dundalk; fair fourth of 13 at 200-1 in a 7f maiden in February; never a threat in a handicap later that month; made a promising start to her turf career when second over 7f at Limerick two weeks ago; not much to choose between her and Dawn Flame who met trouble in running
Laytown winner in 2024 and won a 7f claimer at Dundalk last December; some fair runs in 7f/1m Dundalk handicaps in the spring; 0-28 record on turf is a significant negative.

Won an early-season 5f Cork maiden last year; did not appear again until March this year; two ordinary Dundalk runs in the spring; has a bit to find with Princess Chloe and Dawn Flame on running at Limerick a fortnight ago.

AW winner over 1m in January; that had seemed like a flash in the pan until a revival in form when overcoming a troubled passage to take third behind the well-fancied Glen Breeze and today's rival Princess Chloe at Limerick; again squeezed for room before keeping on for fifth at Leopardstown last week; fair chance with a little more luck.

11-race maiden; regressive in handicaps for the Slattery team last season; down from a peak of 72 to a modest 47 now; possible that a change of scene will do the trick; Conor O'Dwyer tries a new headgear combination.
Seven wins between turf and AW over 5f-6f for his previous trainers; made a bright start for this stable when fourth over 6f at Fairyhouse last month; mid-division in two more recent outings.
Very hard to take encouragement from three maiden runs; in good hands and may do much better in handicaps.

Almost three years since he last ran on turf and has a better overall record on AW; missed 2024 and 2025; pleasing reappearance at Wolverhampton in March; doubts raised by subsequent form; new headgear combination now.

Sole win from 22 starts came at Listowel last summer (off 40); fair sixth at the same venue in May on seasonal debut; perhaps unlucky not to finish closer when 5l sixth of 13 at Killarney ten days ago, had to be wait to get a clear run.

OwnerName: Hugh J O'Brien & Colm O'Brien & Ms Denise McCourt
Spotlight: Has been running over longer trips; improved slightly on moderate form when fifth at Down Royal last month; had only one behind in a 1m3f Naas contest last time.
Best run this season was over 5f on soft ground when second from out of the handicap at Down Royal; has done plenty of racing lately and has become unreliable.

Placed in a couple of 7f/1m handicaps last October on soft/heavy off basement mark; labouring this season and impossible to fancy on recent showings; last of nine in a claimer at Ballinrobe on Monday.
Weak form in maidens; towards the back in handicaps at Leopardstown and Killarney; 2lb out of the handicap.

Losing run up to 16; has run some fine races in that period but her hold-up style dictates that things need to drop right and she got going too late when third in 1m Pontefract Listed race 18 days ago; prior to that she finished around 2l behind the reopposing Kon Tiki when eighth of 15 to Blue Bolt in the Duke Of Cambridge over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm).
Won this race on good ground 12 months ago but was on an upward curve at that stage and doesn't obviously arrive in anything like the same form this time round.

Missed the rest of the season after finishing seventh in the Coronation over C&D at 2025 Royal Ascot but has returned with two fine runs behind Blue Bolt, latterly when fourth of 15 in the Duke Of Cambridge over C&D (good to firm); the one likely to give Touleen most to do.

Came up well short in Group 1/Listed events in the second half of 2025 but different story on Kempton AW reappearance, readily seeing off ten rivals in 1m Listed race; something presumably not right when favourite for an Epsom Group 3 on Derby day (good to soft), finishing a distant last of seven; given seven weeks to get over that.

Improved upon her 2yo form when coming from the back of the pack to beat Touleen and win the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good) on her reappearance; bounced back from a tame effort in the Irish 1,000 Guineas at the Curragh when sixth of nine to Precise in the Coronation over C&D last month but Touleen was 2.5l ahead of her in second on that occasion.

Stepped up on reappearance form when winning Listed event over 1m2f at Newbury (good) in May; can probably be forgiven her subsequent effort in the Prix de Diane at Chantilly after pressing the pace out wide; drops back to 1m now; even a return to her best probably won't be enough, though.

Highly tried last season, showing pretty smart form when second in Leopardstown Group 3 and when beaten under 4l in Group 1 Moyglare at the Curragh; dropped to maiden company to edge out subsequent Oaks winner Thundering On on 1m Leopardstown reappearance; off since but evidently capable when fresh and likely to have a say if handling the quicker ground (raced on good or softer so far).

Edged out by Sukanya in the Fred Darling at Newbury on reappearance but had that reopposing rival behind her when an improved second to Precise in the Group 1 Coronation over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting; even better than the result (met trouble a few times) on that occasion and a similar level of performance will make her hard to beat back in a Group 3.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: Competitive in some of his handicaps in Ireland after winning a 7f maiden at Galway a year ago; left Jessica Harrington for 33,000gns; should pay his way for new connections off this sort of mark.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: Win number three in seven starts this year when always prominent and collecting by a length at Beverley (7.4f); that was in a good time and he's only 2lb higher; clear claims from a good draw.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: Unraced here; arrives in a fair run of form and although only four ran when second at Catterick (7f, good to firm; new visor), the winner was an unexposed 3yo; likely to have some say from the inside stall.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: No further progress since his successful yard debut over Hamilton's extended 1m in May and others look on better terms with the handicapper.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: Four AW wins from 5f to 7f; good sixth of 12 at York (6f, good) before scuppered by the widest stall over 7f here four weeks ago; better boxed this afternoon and she likes to be handy in her races; interesting.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: Won a four-runner novice at Ascot (7f, soft) in September 2024; well handicapped on some of his form but needs to rediscover a spark.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time AW winner who is 0-12 on turf but was very competitive in his last two races here, beaten a short head (7f) and then faring best of those who chased a strong pace two weeks ago (C&D); firmly in the mix.

RaceName: Tom Jones Live On 14th August Handicap
Spotlight: No wins in 11 but denied by a neck in his last two races, both over 7f at Musselburgh and Carlisle; if handling this track then should feature off an untouched mark.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Nine wins in a varied career include this race 12 months ago and a Group 1 in Saudi Arabia (10.5f, good to firm) in February; far from disgraced in Hong Kong last time and now returns from three months off; should give his running but a 5lb penalty makes the task more difficult.

Second to Pride Of Arras in last year's Dante over C&D; looked set for a stellar 2026 when trouncing five rivals in Group 3 at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on reappearance, but hasn't repeated the form in 1m Group 1s since; stepping back up in distance looks a sensible move and he's the one to beat judged on that standout Newmarket effort.

Most recent success came in Group 2 at Sandown (1m, good) last April; not at best in three runs this season, including in same race and when returned to 1m2f for Group 1 at Royal Ascot five weeks ago; needs a revival.

Has an unblemished record at York, winning the Dante (1m2f) and Great Voltigeur (1m4f) last season; had a delayed start to 2026 due to a bruised foot and almost certainly needed the run when last of eight in the Group 1 Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud three weeks ago; interesting with that outing behind him and back on the Knavesmire.

Beat subsequent Derby winner Christmas Day in the Group 2 Dante over C&D (good ground) in May, only to finish well beaten behind that rival on much softer ground at Epsom (11-2); still low-mileage and looked potentially top-class in the Dante; may get back on track on today's forecast firmer ground.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Stepped up on his Ripon debut third when winning a 6f novice at Hamilton in May; ten-week absence and the fitting of a tongue tie are slight concerns but he is bred to carry on improving.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Travelled strongly and picked up well to record a snug success in a 5f novice at Nottingham (5f, good) in April; gelded last month;   open to improvement and 6f should suit well.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Too green to do himself justice at Newmarket on debut in May but he took a significant step forward with his defeat of 17 rivals at Newbury (6f, good to firm) 16 days ago; from the family of Battaash and there should be more under the bonnet.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Had a subsequent nursery winner back in second when winning at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) last month; capable of better but that was only a Band D event and this will demand more.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Some promise when fourth of six at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; others look stronger all the same.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: He made a promising start to his career when third of six at York (5f, good) in May; strong favourite for a Ripon novice last month on the strength of it but he was impeded over 1f out and couldn't show his true colours; remains with potential.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 62,000euros yearling; second foal; dam a 7f 2yo/1m2f Listed winner (RPR 98); may need further in time but he is still a newcomer to note for market confidence.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 38,000gns yearling, £55,000 breeze-up 2yo; first foal; dam 1m-1m2f AW maiden (RPR 62), closely related to winners Scintiulla (1m1f Group 3), Cuis Ghaire (6f 2yo Group 3) and Gile Na Greine (smart 7f 2yo); neither of the stable's 2yo winners this year have won first time out.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ninth foal; brother to Italian winners The King's Horses (5f-1m including 2yo Listed) and Time Of Rebirth (6f-1m1f including 2yo), closely related to 2m hurdle winner Chingachook; dam unraced half-sister to 5f Group 3 winner Astrophysical Jet; apprentice-ridden on debut.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 7,000euros yearling, £27,000 breeze-up 2yo; sixth foal; half-sister to winners Surrey Blaze (8.6f-1m4f; RPR 81), Arctic Blaze (10.6f AW/12.5f turf; 71) and Better Not Bitter (Australian (6f-1m1f); dam maiden half-sister to useful 7f-1m4f winner Adjaliya; one of three runners for Brian Ellison.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 33-1 when finishing down the field at Redcar (6f, good to firm) in May; a big step forward is necessary.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 10,000euros yearling, resold 16,000gns yearling, 65,000euros breeze-up 2yo; fifth foal; half-sister to winners Enceladus (10.4f/1m4f; RPR 100) and Moab (1m6f AW; 75); dam prolific US 7f-8.5f winner (including Grade 2; 112); looks the part on paper; betting to guide.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Two runs last month, showing better form on the second occasion; even that effort is still well short of the required standard here.

RaceName: Say When Gosforth And Ponteland EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C & D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fifth foal; half-sister to Swedish 1m winner Crack Up Gaudelius; dam 6f/7f winner (including 2yo/AW; RPR 83), half-sister to Italian 7.5f winner Rekindled Amore; one of three for Brian Ellison.
Has failed to reach the first three in 11 attempts; has shown his best form this season in two Curragh outings; well beaten at Leopardstown last time (7f, good); blinkers go on now.

Four-time winner but last win came in a claimer in 2024; some satisfactory efforts this season and the best of them came last time at Leopardstown (7f, good) when taking the runner-up spot; in the mix.

Sole win came in a Brighton maiden in September 2024; has been regressive over various trips this season; not his worst effort when mid-field in a Killarney claimer (1m, good) last time; others preferred.
Veteran winner of 14 races (11 on AW); shaped well in his four races this season, the latest when a 4.5l fifth of 15 at Roscommon (7.5f, good), weakening late on; should go well once again.

OwnerName: Ms Julianne McNally & Colette McNally & D McNally
Spotlight: Five career wins, the last two coming at Listowel; best run this term came last month at Roscommon (7.5f, good) when a never-nearer fourth; didn't progress at Killarney last time (1m, good) when keen.

Sprang a surprise in a three-runner rated race at Dundalk in February (6f); has beaten few rivals in three runs since; some reasons to be hopeful are a recent gelding operation, a first run in 0-60 company and the presence of Browne McMonagle in the saddle for the first time.

Fourth here on seasonal return in April (1m, soft) and back to form on second handicap start when staying on to be runner-up to subsequent winner Rodeo Drive at Ballinrobe (1m2f, yielding); well beaten at Killarney last time when trying 1m4f for the first time; best form on easier ground.

Placed in two of his previous three starts against older horses before gaining a first win back against his own age group at Limerick last time (6.5f, good); up 9lb for that win, but should continue to give a good account of himself; badly drawn, though.

OwnerName: Ms Denise McCourt & Stephen Sweeney & Maire Bailey
Spotlight: Didn't improve for the switch to handicaps at Bellewstown (1m, good) when 19.5l behind the winner; dual headgear is reached for in the search for more.
Made a decent handicap debut at Roscommon in June when slowly away before keeping on into sixth over an extended 7f; never on terms at Limerick last time (6.5f, good); others more likely.
AW maiden winner in 2024; one good run last year, a 0.5l second of 13 at Limerick in July; poor return at Fairyhouse in May (6f, good); needs to improve hugely on that.
Beaten by 29l on stable debut at Bellewstown when 8lb out of the weights; this is a more suitable leve,l but others appeal more despite the first-time hood.

Winless from 23 starts; ran his best race on turf in this race (good) last year when a 1.5l third off 7lb higher; satisfactory efforts at Fairyhouse over 6f in his last two runs; not ruled out, but drawn wide.
Towards the rear in all three maidens, the latter two at triple-figure prices; may improve for handicaps now.
Best run for previous yard came when fourth in a Down Royal nursery off 61 in September; struggled in five starts for new connections, including when beaten 22l at Naas earlier this month.

Won back-to-back handicaps on the AW at Dundalk in November/January over 6f/7f, the latter off a mark of 45; her 3.75l third at Killarney (1m, good) last time was her best effort on turf; 3lb wrong but she could find enough improvement in first-time cheekpieces.

Below his best on his last two runs, most recently over C&D at the Royal meeting; has some good C&D form, however, such as when fourth in both this race last year and the Victoria Cup in May; not ruled out each-way.

Returned to form when dropped back in trip in first-time cheekpieces (retained) in the Wokingham here (6f, good to firm) last month, finishing fast under Ryan Moore for a head second; on that evidence the return to 7f could be a good move and he's one to consider.

Merely mid-division behind Aalto in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket a fortnight ago but this C&D brings out the best in him, as evidenced by this season's close-up finishes in the Victoria Cup (good) and Buckingham Palace Stakes (good to firm); could be bang there now back at Ascot.

Won this last year (good) and followed up in the Stewards' Cup at Goodwood (6f, good to soft); after a very good start to this year at Meydan he hasn't hit the same heights since; his recent seventh in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket was a step back in the right direction but he needs another today.

5yo who produced a career-best performance with authoritative win at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; following a 9lb rise he was well beaten over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting 12 days later, finishing fourth of six in the unfavoured far-side group, but he's not written off.

Reappeared with a win in the Spring Mile at Doncaster (good to soft) before good third at Newbury (1m, good), and took another step forward to win the Buckingham Palace over C&D (good to firm) at Royal Ascot; this 4yo is clearly progressive and could play another leading role up 4lb for last time.

Reappeared with a convincing handicap win at Newbury (7f, good) in April; underwhelming favourite in Listed races at Newmarket and Epsom on next two starts but gelded since and returns to a handicap this afternoon, and he could have a part to play if rediscovering the Newbury form.

Admirably consistent in defeat this term and he was a close second to Aalto in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) recently; races off the same mark today (due a 2lb rise) and could again be thereabouts.

Novice wins on his first two starts and he made it 3-3 when winning a big-field handicap at York (7f, good) last month, doing it comfortably despite having to wait for a run; there is a strong suspicion he's a Group-race winner in the making and he could take an 8lb rise in his stride.

Beaten on his last 16 starts and this hold-up horse needs things to drop right, which didn't happen at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last Saturday when he was a close fifth of nine having been denied a clear run; however, he's on an attractive mark if getting the breaks and Jamie Spencer, who excels on the straight course here, is on board for the first time.

Won early this year on first three runs for James Horton (7f/1m, AW) before good third here (1m, good to firm) and a fifth of seven at Sandown (1m, good); won at Kempton (1m, AW) next time; could give a good account but he's 6-9 on AW as opposed to 0-10 on turf, which tempers enthusiasm.

Two wins last term (1m/7f, AW/good) and he added another on his reappearance at Haydock (7f, good) in May; again ran well when fourth of 15 at Newbury (7f, good to soft) latest but his form needs to go to a new level today.

His career-best efforts have come in the last three runnings of the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket (7f, good/good to firm), winning it in 2024 and a fortnight ago with a near-miss in between; under a 3lb penalty there's still mileage in his mark but he's never finished better than ninth from four visits here.

Inconsistent sort who is opposable on the majority of his form over the last 12 months and was only sixth at Newmarket last time; however, he's popped up with the odd big run, finishing third in this last year and filling the same position in a big field at York last month; not a forlorn hope each-way.

Won in first-time cheekpieces (retained since) at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) in April and has continued in good heart on his two outings since; however, he's up in grade this afternoon and needs something extra.

Denied a clear run when fifth at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) latest and he's a type who needs things to drop right; however, he got up on the line at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) two runs ago and may have an each-way shout.

Won at Kempton (6f, AW) last month before near-miss at Epsom (6f, good), and back on the scoresheet with ready win here (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; under a 3lb penalty this progressive 3yo is 5lb ahead of the handicapper today, and he showed promise over 7f last season; major player.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins on the AW but he's just as effective on turf; needs to bounce back from a poor run at Newmarket's July meeting but he's down sharply in grade here and his form from the spring has a solid look to it.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Campaigned solely at 7f this term but shapes as if he'll be well suited by this return to 1m; has met trouble in running on his last two starts; thrown in on the pick of his form for Richard Hannon and could be ready to strike.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Sprang a 33-1 surprise on stable debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in January, and back to form when second at Ascot (1m, good to firm) two weeks ago; should be thereabouts.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Front-runner with a favourable low draw; shaped nicely at Newmarket (1m, good) on reappearance and quick ground was blamed for a poor run next time; below the mark of his last win (over C&D) and no surprise if he makes a bold bid from the front, especially if the rain materialises.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
OwnerName: S Bulmer, P Hebdon & R Taylor
Spotlight: Had slipped in the weights before winning at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) on Sunday; not certain to be as effective back at 1m and he's ridden by an apprentice with a smaller claim.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Won two from five last season and looks as good as ever this term, fourth in a big field at Ascot two weeks ago; effective at 7f and 1m; should be in the thick of things again.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
OwnerName: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde
Spotlight: Consistent type who won six times last season and arrives on the back of two close seconds; this race looks deeper than his last two but he's in fine form and unlikely to be far away.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Far more miss than hit this season and beat only one home at Newmarket last time; others preferred.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Had been bubbling under prior to winning easily at Redcar (1m, good to firm) on Sunday, and given the style of that success he looks an attractive proposition under a 5lb penalty; high on the list.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Has a better strike-rate on AW than grass but she's in better form than her last two turf runs suggest, short of room at Ascot on latest; less obvious than several of these but not ruled out.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; hasn't had the rub of the green of late, repeatedly denied a run when stepped up to 1m at Newcastle four weeks ago; respected.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Falling in the weights and ran respectably when third to Rajapour at Redcar on Sunday, but the winner bolted up that day and it's hard to see the tables being turned.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Upped markedly in trip here (1m6f) four weeks ago and predictably failed to stay; previous form (7f-1m1f) is solid enough but a wide draw could be difficult to overcome.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Arrives on a recent high after a win at Musselburgh and a second at Ripon (both 1m, good); should give his running but he's up in grade here.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Just three wins but has been second or third 17 times, including on his last four starts; stall 17 could be tricky.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Nosed home at Redcar (1m, good) in May and ran creditably when a close third at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) two weeks ago; her mark is unchanged but she's up from a 0-65 to a 0-80.

RaceName: IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Three defeats include a seller and he's earned himself a low handicap mark; now gelded.

RaceName: IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 250-1 when a tailed-off last over 7f at Carlisle a month ago.

RaceName: IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: £62,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; doesn't look an imminent winner after his first two efforts and probably one for handicaps.

RaceName: IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Lengthy odds for both his runs over 7f on the AW; they finished in a heap when he went close at Southwell and he was outpaced when it mattered at Lingfield; however, there are positives to take from those efforts and he surely has more to offer.

RaceName: IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Well related; looks to have been learning on the job and again shaped encouragingly when beaten 5l in a useful 7f novice at Sandown (good); has to improve on that but he will at some stage.

RaceName: IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 38,000gns yearling; Lope Y Fernandez half-brother to five winners; shaped with considerable promise when third at Newmarket in what is always a strong maiden (7f, good to firm); wasn't helped by his track position, either; hard to beat.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Fairly useful 1m winner in 2025; back on track when runner-up in handicaps (around 1m) at Thirsk and Epsom this summer but only eighth at Sandown (1m) last time; needs to bounce back.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Landed 1m novices on his first two starts in 2025; signed off for Hugo Palmer with a good second of ten in 1m Kempton handicap 23 days ago; changed hands for 30,000 guineas and not out of things for new handler.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Debut course winner for William Haggas; failed to build on encouraging reappearance Redcar sixth for new stable when only eighth of 11 over C&D 30 days ago; needs to get back on track.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Signed off for 2025 with a third C&D success in September but he's yet to fire this season, last of 14 over C&D in April; has it to prove after a break.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Ex-French gelding who made a winning handicap debut on AW at Lingfield (1m) in May; tongue tied when good third in 1m Kempton handicap last time; has few miles still on the clock and may do better still; likely player.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Debut 1m Navan maiden winner for Dermot Weld last autumn; off seven months before a fading fourth of five in 7f Newmarket novice for new yard 30 days ago; sent off evens there, and remains with potential now going handicapping.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Bagged Yarmouth maiden and Redcar novice (both 7f) last autumn; cheekpieces fitted and right back on track of late, a close sixth of nine in 1m1f Musselburgh handicap 25 days ago; in the mix on his Tapeta debut with blinkers added.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: On a losing sequence and he was a below-par fifth of nine in 1m Nottingham handicap last month; others are preferred.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Looked on the up when landing 1m Pontefract handicap in April but failed to build on it when third of five at Nottingham (1m) last month; still low mileage and not written off.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Ended 2025 with C&D victory and he's advanced his form this season, posting good third of 14 in 1m Kempton handicap 26 days ago; cheekpieces added; merits consideration from an unchanged mark.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Improving son of Zoustar who gained a first win (at the fourth attempt) in 7f novice here 29 days ago; yard took this 12 months ago, and he's open to further progress stepping up to 1m for his handicap debut; interesting.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Zelzal colt who landed 1m Thirsk novice in April; well-held seventh of nine on handicap debut at Chester (1m2f) last month; tongue tied here and worth another chance after just three starts.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Bagged a fourth C&D success in February; off since a below-par seventh over C&D in March though so needs to hit the ground running.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Made a winning return in 7f AW handicap at Lingfield in April and posted a solid fifth of 14 over C&D last month; remains low mileage and not ruled out for yard among the winners.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Won a 7f Curragh maiden last June in his only race as a 2yo; twice second in small-field races but was beginning to look limited until producing a smart display to take second in the 1m2f Golden Gates Stakes (Handicap) at Royal Ascot; overtook Nil Bua Gan Dua in the closing stages and can emerge best in the rematch.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Handed a rating of 88 after a 1m5f maiden win at Leopardstown on his third outing; will need to improve to feature in a race of this standard.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: A K Whelan & Reeves Thoroughbred Racing
Spotlight: Highly tried in Pattern races as a juvenile; off the mark when making all over an extended 1m2f at Roscommon on seasonal debut this term; only 1 3/4l behind the stronger-finishing Amadeus Mozart when fourth of 16 on handicap debut at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); proved vulnerable over a longer trip in the 1m5f Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket; cheekpieces on now.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Rectory Road Hldgs Ltd/E Palmer/W Slattery/Mrs A M O'Brien
Spotlight: Wide-margin winner on heavy ground at Tipperary on debut last October; creditable fifth behind Pierre Bonnard in Group 1 at Saint-Cloud only three weeks later; soundly beaten in two Group 3s this season and well beaten in a 1m5f handicap last time; plenty to prove now; tongue-tie fitted

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to Melbourne Cup winner Gold Trip; second to the subsequent Irish Oaks winner Johanna Walsh over 1m2f at Leopardstown in May after making her debut at Dundalk in April; returned to AW to record a wide-margin maiden win; held her own when a fine third in Royal Ascot's King George V Stakes (Handicap); further progress likely.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Beat an 86-rated previous winner in a 1m contest at Dundalk in December on her only juvenile start; set a tough task in a fillies' Group 3 event at Navan on return; struggled in a valuable race at this venue last time; up against it.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Course maiden winner on her second start; deserves a shot at this after a Killarney handicap win; progressive filly; needs to find extra to trouble a trio with Royal Ascot handicap form.

RaceName: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Deserved her breakthrough win at Killarney after three consecutive placed efforts; can prove useful in a lower grade; much inferior to her two stablemates on figures.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: His flop in the Coronation Cup at Epsom last month can be excused by the substantial rain and he showed he was none the worse when winning the Group 1 Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; had just a neck to spare last time but did well to come from the back of the pack off a stop-start gallop; he's a six-time winner at the top level, including of this race last year, and holds leading claims.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Resolute Bloodstock & Philip Baron Von Ullmann
Spotlight: Won this in 2024 (good to firm) at 25-1 and has won four Group races since, the latest the Group 2 Grand Prix de Chantilly (1m4f, good) this May; bang there in the final furlong of the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting only for Christophe Soumillon to lose his irons; he has an each-way chance.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Last season's Derby and Irish Derby winner who reappeared with a win in the Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester in May; however, he hasn't come up to scratch on his three starts since and needs to turn things around; the cheekpieces worn on his four outings this season are left off.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Won the Grade 1 Tenno Sho (Autumn) at Tokyo (1m2f, good to firm) last November and narrowly lost out to Calandagan in a titanic tussle in the Grade 1 Japan Cup there (1m4f, good to firm) later that month; bumped into prolific Grade 1 winner Romantic Warrior when second in the Grade 1 QEII Cup at Sha Tin (1m2f, good to firm) in April on his sole run this year and this Japanese raider could have a big part to play in his rematch with Calandagan.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: 6yo who produced a clear career best when beaten a nose at 206-1 in the Grade 1 Tenno Sho (Spring) at Kyoto (2m, good to firm) in May; however, on a formline through the winner he has something to find with Calandagan and compatriot Masquerade Ball.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: She's won the last two runnings of the Group 1 British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes here in October and she was a 1l second of five to Calandagan in this race last year; short-headed in the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting and she might not be far away.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: 1m4f Group 1 wins last summer in the Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks before head second in the 1m4f Arc at Longchamp; back on song when runner-up in the Group 1 Prince of Wales's Stakes here (1m2f, good to firm) last month and, although she was beaten 4l and Ryan Moore rides stablemate Benvenuto Cellini today, she was behind the brilliant Ombudsman and could build on that latest effort now she's back up to 1m4f.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Runner-up in the Group 1 Futurity Trophy at Doncaster (1m, heavy) last October and filled the same position in the Group 2 Dante at York (10.2f, good) in May; however, he's been well beaten in the Derby and Irish Derby on his last two starts, having made the running; hard to fancy.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Favourite in the rain-affected Derby at Epsom last month, when he finished tenth past the post but was deemed to be a non-runner having got his leg caught in the stalls; subsequently justified favouritism in the Irish Derby at the Curragh (1m4f, good); this is a tougher test of his credentials but he brings star potential and he's Ryan Moore's mount of the Ballydoyle four; he may well be up to the task.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: N Bradley Racing 29, D Scott & P Spencer
Spotlight: Overcame slow start to win comfortably at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month; open to further progress and should be just as effective back at 6f, but carries a penalty in what looks a stronger race.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Did her best work late on after a slow start when sixth at Newmarket (6f, good to firm; 17-2) two weeks ago, finishing a place behind Hout Bay; like that rival, she could make quite a bit of progress for the experience.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: 200,000gns yearling; too green to do herself justice (slowly away, flashed tail soon after start) when fifth on debut over C&D (6-1) earlier this month; plenty of improvement required but she might have learned a lot.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
Spotlight: 150,000euros breeze-up buy; went off 50-1 but shaped nicely when fifth of 11 at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago, rallying after being short of room; could improve significantly and commands major respect.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Seemed to know her job and shaped encouragingly when 1l third of nine at Redcar (6f, good to firm; 5-2) in May, always up with the pace; that form is probably nothing special but she's in good hands and should progress.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: £50,000 yearling, £75,000 breeze-up 2yo; by Mehmas; dam Group-placed 7f/1m winner (including 2yo; RPR 108), out of US 8.5f Grade 2 winner; upwardly mobile stable had its first 2yo winner of the season earlier this month; well worth a market check.

Impressive on debut at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) last May and tapped back into that promise when short-headed in a handicap at Meydan (6f, good) in March (gelded after); raced too freely and weakened from prominence in top 3yo handicap at York (6f, good) on British return six weeks ago; hopefully the addition of a hood helps him to settle better this time.

Dual C&D novice winner last season and his handicap form this year is strong, finishing fourth in the Palace Of Holyroodhouse at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) before returning to 6f to finish a neck second of 13 to Jazl in a traditionally hot race at the Newmarket July meeting (good to firm again); a 2lb nudge doesn't look enough to stop him from a good draw.

Going the right way, making it 2-2 since dropping to 6f when seeing off six rivals on course handicap debut (good) a fortnight ago; has the potential for better again but he was able to control that race from the front from the inside stall and hasn't fared so well with the draw this time.

Made all for wide-margin win on his debut at Lingfield (AW) in November and he was back around that sort of form when second to the very promising Behike (second in strong Ascot handicap recently) in good-ground novice there (also 6f) in May; interesting runner.

Third Chester success when beating older horses over 5f (good to soft; has won on good to firm) last month; never involved behind Calico Blue in the Palace Of Holyroodhouse at Royal Ascot since but his 1131 course record suggests a much better run is likely now.
Her reappearance second of 17 at the York Dante meeting (good) is strong form but she's failed to back it up twice since; races beyond 5f for the first time now; drawn widest.

Good second in sales and Listed races over 6f at York during his 2yo campaign but not in anything like the same form this term; sold out of the Richard & Peter Fahey stable for 26,000gns since his latest start four weeks ago.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Has beaten just a couple of rivals in each of two 1m4f starts; can be ruled out in this clash with the younger generation.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Cheap yearling; fifth foal; half-sister by Bobby's Kitten to two winners who stayed further than this; dam 7f AW winner.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Has changed stable since a fair fifth of 16 on debut at Limerick; open to improvement; likely to need more experience.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Has shown little in two runs over an extended 1m2f; cheekpieces tried now by top trainer; may improve but best watched until she shows a spark of promise.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Half-sister to the smart Princess Child who was a Group 3 winner for this stable last season; ran once on AW last season; champion jockey prefers Vishaya.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Wootton Bassett filly made some late headway on debut at Leopardstown; perhaps a little unlucky not to peg back a front-running 50-1 chance at Naas in May; confirmed maiden-winning potential with third of 19 at the same venue; seems likely to uphold form with the more exposed Wearing Stars who took fourth place

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Soundly beaten in third behind a high-class Joseph O'Brien-trained runner at Limerick on debut; likely to need more experience.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Has struggled in two races at Limerick; 5 1/2l behind Hello Stacia on the second occasion.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Lovely pedigree (dam won a Group 1); has not yet shown enough to suggest she is a likely maiden winner.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: David K Kelly & Mrs Pauline Condon
Spotlight: Rated 77; some solid efforts in defeat; bounced back from a disappointing handicap run at the Curragh when second in a claimer at Roscommon and has continued to show similar form in maidens; needs to raise her game a notch.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Placed in two AW maidens early this year; modest run on turf debut in 1m Naas maiden (good); narrowly denied by in-form rival off 74 on handicap debut at Killarney 12 days ago; officially rated 7lb inferior to Elmakaya.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Twice placed over 6f on AW late last year; fourth in 5f Cork maiden on reappearance; never in contention on handicap debut; better when stepped up to 7f in a Down Royal maiden; finished 1 1/4l behind Elmakaya at Naas; more exposed than that rival, good place chance all the same.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Second foal; half-sister by Starman to a three-time minor winner; dam, by War Command, an unraced half-sister to two useful winners; fitted with cheekpieces for debut.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: A useful 1m winner at his best for Jack Channon; offered little in two runs for Brian Toomey this spring though and came in last of 14 for John Butler in 7f handicap here four weeks ago; no surprise if he took a step forward though with new yard among the winners.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: On a long losing run but a useful AW performer at his best; off 7 months before coming in only 11th in 1m1f York handicap on his return last month but this C&D winner bounce back.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo who went 2-4 when scoring on his handicap debut at Kempton (1m) in January, despite conceding first run; off since but he remains very much one to be interested in with Billy Loughnane up.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
OwnerName: Castle View, A Bell, S Oliver & M Severs
Spotlight: Fair bumper winner; got off the mark on his third Flat start in 7f Carlisle novice in May and not discredited with eighth of 16 in 1m1f York handicap last month; respected on his Tapeta debut.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Took this in 2025 and also scored over C&D in February; not at her best when 11th over C&D last time but she's the sort to bounce back.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: A two-time 7f scorer last September; posted a good third at Haydock (7f) in May but beat just one in 1m Nottingham handicap last month; needs to get back on track.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Looked on the up in a trio of 1m AW novices (scored at Southwell) in the spring; run best ignored (badly hampered under 2f out) when last on turf debut in 7.5f Chester handicap last month; remains with potential returned to Tapeta with cheekpieces fitted.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: C&D winner who comes here on the back of a good second of five in 1m Doncaster handicap last month, just failing; not out of things despite a 2lb weights rise.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: On a losing run but posted his best effort for new stable with third of nine in 7.5f Chester handicap two weeks ago; in the mix if taking another step forward.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: A fair 1m1f winner in 2025 but arrives out of sorts, beating one in 1m handicap at Pontefract eight days ago; others are preferred.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Dual winner (including here) in 2025 but his more recent turf form is much less encouraging; needs to bounce back returned to Tapeta.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Kickstarted 2026 with 5f win here but his form has nosedived since; it's easy to look elsewhere.

RaceName: Brack Burger On Uber Eats Beeswing Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Winless since 2024 (over C&D) but runner-up in 1m handicaps here on his last two starts; can't be dismissed despite being 3lb out of the handicap.

OwnerName: Gee Gees Racing, P Gleeson & N Barnes
Spotlight: Won at Windsor, Lingfield (11.6f) and Yarmouth in May/June in his first three handicaps, before tailed off on rain-hit ground at Epsom and well beaten with cheekpieces added at York; no headgear today; not proven over quite this far and may have to resume improvement.

Won twice in 2024 for Jane Chapple-Hyam; spent a year with Jack Morland and got off the mark for him at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) 19 days ago; sold again for 22,000gns one day later and this is his first run back with his former yard; back up 4lb and not proven beyond an extended 1m2f (unraced over this far); tongue-tie and headgear worn for his last yard is removed; quite a few questions, but peak 2024 form was a bit better.

Second of five last term in his only race on good to firm; won at Salisbury in May and improved again when a close second at Goodwood (again 1m4f on good) in June; the Goodwood winner scored again next time but this 4yo has been raised just 1lb and is heading the right way; big shout.

Has won six races on the Flat at up to 1m6f and this year is going particularly well, with two hurdle wins and now two over about 1m4f on Flat (on good ground at Salisbury and Chester); raised 4lb to career-high mark but should be fine back on good to firm and he's never been better.

Last won when sharing the spoils at Southwell (1m4f, AW) in April 2025; close second of 15 at Newbury (1m4f, good) in May was his best show this season and he acts on good to firm, but others are preferred for win purposes; this is a very rare run in headgear.
