Acts on good to firm; in good form over 1m6f/2m last June, including for a Chester win off 3lb lower than today; well held on sole start here (last July) and not seen since last September; he ran well first time out last season but others look more persuasive today.

Turf wins this term at Bath (1m), Chepstow (1m4f) and Leicester (1m2f), with one of those under Ashley Lewis; however, her form has dropped off somewhat in 1m4f races on last two outings and this race demands more.

2-21 on turf and 3-21 on AW, with latest win in March; usually seen over shorter; her last turf run was last September and that 2025 turf campaign went the wrong way, but at least she has a lower mark this time.
Wore cheekpieces last three outings, for a rallying second at Sandown (1m2f, good/good to firm) on last two occasions; better is needed but he shapes as if new trip is well worth a go.

2yo win was over 1m on soft at a stiff track and he was stepped up to 1m4f when second of four at Chepstow (good to firm) on latest outing, his best show this term; needs to build on that but he saw the trip out very well and could have more in the tank.

Two seconds and two thirds from his six starts; upped to 1m2f then 11.4f in handicaps for his two starts this season, best form in a never-nearer second of five last time; back up 2lb but could have more to give at this trip.

Below form sole start on good to firm; made the frame on all his four runs as 2yo, short-headed in a 1m1f maiden on final outing; cheekpieces were added for handicap/seasonal debut at Kempton (1m3f, AW) and he wasn't beaten far but hung right and came last of five; off 115 days since (gelded) and needs overall improvement.

Won maiden at Ripon (1m2f, good) in April; contested three small-field handicaps since, finishing third on last two occasions (1m4f/1m6f); while a return to 1m4f may help, she needs to raise her game.

1m6f and/or soft ground may excuse his latest start, when he raced freely in the lead in first-time cheekpieces; previously showed some ability over about 1m4f but more is needed, particularly as he is 5lb out of the handicap; tongue-tie is added and 7lb claimer is also recruited.

Ex-Irish; has done much better for new yard, including wins (1m2f, good to firm) under Jack Doughty at Chepstow and Leicester before her creditable fifth of ten at Wolverhampton (upped to 1m4f, AW); position 9lb out of the handicap this time, however, demands a leap forward.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Could be unexposed at 1m4f and ran creditably on first attempt at trip when third of eight at Ascot (good to firm) two weeks ago; goes well for positive tactics and Toby Moore's 7lb claim is a bonus.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Bred to be useful and has been steadily progressive; clearcut winner at Lingfield (1m4f) towards end of 2025 and shaped well over inadequate 1m2f at Chester (good) on reappearance; this step back up in distance should be perfect and she has rock-solid claims.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 7yo; has an impressive strike-rate but all six of his wins have come on the AW and he hasn't been placed in four runs on turf; below par last time and has a fair bit to prove.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Hasn't been long with David O'Meara and he looks to be building up to something, bumping in to an improver when second of 12 at Ayr (1m5f, soft) five weeks ago; quick ground would be an unknown but otherwise he has plenty in his favour.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Useful 3yo when based in France, largely disappointing for Joseph O'Brien last year; some promise for current yard, not helped by racing wide at Chester (1m2f) last time; moves into unknown territory trip-wise but his mark is falling and he's impossible to discount.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Arrives on a hat-trick after 1m3f AW wins for Andrew Balding at Kempton and Southwell, after which he was sold for 50,000gns; not fully proven on turf, although he did show promise at Haydock on his debut; has joined a very capable stable and may not have reached his ceiling just yet.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Awarded C&D Queen Mother's Cup last June and much lower in the weights now, but that's because his form has fallen off a cliff; dangerous if blinkers (replacing other headgear) spark a revival but carries clear risks.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Represents a new trainer in excellent form and has won at Goodwood (1m4f, good) and Epsom (1m4f, good to firm) on his last two outings, proving himself better than ever; edging up the weights only gradually and in the mix again.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Formerly trained by Andrew Balding and Nicky Henderson; sole Flat win came over 1m2f in 2023 but she has since won five times over hurdles; ran creditably over 2m at Lingfield at the start of the year before being sold for £6,000 in May; worth a check in the market.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: On a long losing run and never a threat here two weeks ago, but he'd previously been beaten just a nose in the Queen Mother's Cup over C&D in June; none too reliable but a danger to all if he's on a going day.

4yo with only six races behind him and has gone 2-3 in handicaps with narrow verdicts at Thirsk and Musselburgh (again 5f, good); essentially 5lb higher than last time as Zak Wheatley claimed 3lb that day, but he's got a good draw and first-time headgear; respected.

All six wins have been here and at Wolverhampton, including this race 12 months ago when 6lb lower; close fourth here last time when drawn wide but in a smaller field than today and now he's out in stall 12; cheekpieces tried last time are removed.

Beat a big field at Thirsk in May and ran pretty well here next time from stall 9 in a Class 3; backed that up with another competitive show and he got himself too far back at York last time; considered.
All wins have been at 5f, the latest by a head at Nottingham in April (1lb lower); disappointing at Newmarket but ran poorly on his previous visit there; could bounce back from a handy draw.

OwnerName: Ms Janelle Cao, Ross Harmon & Partner
Spotlight: Has won twice on the AW since finishing well held in this 12 months ago but hasn't offered all that much in his last three races.
Made all from stall 2 here a fortnight ago under Myla Coppins; she's up in class and the weights (raised 6lb), while stall 7 isn't absolutely ideal.
Fifth AW win in May but only fifth here two weeks ago, extending losing sequence on turf to 11; in fairness, he didn't get much luck through the race but he's stuck out in stall 10.

Admirable veteran who had a wicked draw in a C&D handicap last month that he'd won three times before; better boxed this time and there was much to like about his previous effort at Thirsk; considered.
Won two Class 5s before a strong-finishing third at this level here last time having been last at one point; however, stall 11 could be a killer.
Last run was underwhelming but she was performing well prior to that in 5f/6f handicaps; on the downside, she's drawn quite wide on her first visit to this track.
Three 5f wins on AW for previous yards; ran well for a long way over C&D in May on debut for this stable and faced a tough task at Epsom's Derby meeting; couldn't dismiss from his handy draw.
Course winner who should be well handicapped now but stall 9 won't make life easy.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Shed the maiden tag at the fourth attempt in a Ballinrobe maiden in June (9.5f, yielding); ran respectably when fifth in her second handicap start in a valuable Leopardstown contest 16 days ago (1m1f, good); dropped 1lb but would probably like to see some rain.

Made the breakthrough at the tenth time of asking at Leopardstown (1m, good) when taking advantage of being at the front of affairs to win by 0.75l, with a couple of these behind; up 7lb and has his chance.

OwnerName: J Kirkland & Mrs J M Ryan
Spotlight: Two-time AW winner; yet to score on turf but hasn't run badly at times; posted an underwhelming effort at Leopardstown (1m, good) last time returning from a break when 6.5l behind the winner Frank Pickle; needs to improve.

Both wins have come over 1m at Killarney; won his maiden there last summer (yielding to soft) and returned there a year later to record a first handicap success (good) off 68 last time; not certain to back it up all the same.

3-18 on turf; low-key start to this campaign, but back on song in his latest two runs over 1m at Leopardstown; beaten a neck there in June off 69 and was a 2.25l third behind Frank Pickle off 73 last time; there might be a few better handicapped than him, but he's in form.

All three wins have been gained at the Curragh and a large portion of his places too; good second over 1m at his favoured venue last month and took that good form on tour to Killarney (1m, good) last time when just 0.75l behind the winner Red Hugh O'Donnell; up 3lb for that effort, but a repeat would see him thereabouts.

Sole win came in an AW 7f maiden at Dundalk in December (7f); had the run of the race in a Curragh premier handicap (1m1f, good) last time but it was still a career-best effort in third; interestingly, Browne McMonagle takes over now.

Never saw another rival when making all at Cork (1m, good) to win by 3l; raised 10lb for that but almost repeated the dose at York two weeks ago when headed late on into second (1m, good to firm); raised another 4lb now, but he's thriving and is firmly in the mix.

Creditable efforts in her opening two AW maidens and her best effort came on the switch to turf at Leopardstown last time when a 6.5l third of 14 (1m, yielding to soft); not totally ruled out on handicap bow.
Doesn't always appear the most resolute in a finish but he is regularly placed and conditions hold no terrors; each-way claims once more.
Won a nursery at Carlisle (7f, soft) off a 15lb higher mark in August 2024; not at the same level last year but starts out for her new yard off a reduced mark; tongue tied; worth a market check.

He has finished second in two of his four starts since returned to Jane Chapple-Hyam; disappointing favourite at Wolverhampton 11 days ago, however, and stamina for this trip has to be taken on trust.

The winner of nine races, including C&D, and arrives in good form having finished second in three of his last four races; did rather throw away his latest start at Leicester though, surging to the lead 1f out but dossing in front and picked off close home; has the ability to win but he will need producing late.
Just one win to his name from 26 starts; lacklustre effort here (6f) last month and underwent wind surgery four days later; handy mark if the operation has the desired effect.

Getting on for two years since his last win but this C&D winner has dropped to a tempting mark and he didn't run badly in a stronger race at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) six weeks ago; apprentice takes off a handy 5lb too; high on the list.
His last two wins have come on Tapeta but over longer trips, the latest (1m3f, Southwell) in March off 3lb lower; could prove vulnerable back at 1m.
14-race maiden; tumbling down the weights and his latest Hamilton run was a little better; still not easily recommend though.
Poor form in five starts for Jack Channon; starts out for new yard (same owners) after 404 days off; hard to recommend.
0-18; eyecatching effort over 6f at Hamilton last month but he has been well beaten twice since; a new visor isn't enough to tempt.
C&D winner; successful at Carlisle last May; solid effort at Southwell in January but little to celebrate since; others bring more pressing claims.
Yet to show any promise in six runs from 6f to 1m3f.

Lightly raced 4yo who has been runner-up in competitive handicaps on three of his four starts since April, most recently in last month's 28-runner Royal Hunt Cup over C&D (good to firm); climbing the weights in defeat but he's nevertheless firmly in calculations.

Inconsistent but he's just 1lb higher than when making all at Chelmsford (1m, AW) last December and he returned from a break with an encouraging third at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago, when again making the running; might not face much opposition for the lead; chance.

Good fifth over C&D in last season's Royal Hunt Cup (good to firm) and he reappeared with a win in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) in March; however, well beaten on both starts since; has to get back on track.

With this visor back on, and back on better ground, he returned to form with a well-backed win at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) a fortnight ago, coming clear with a runner-up who was returning from a long absence and won at Sandown on Thursday; an 8lb rise might not stop him.

Won at Kempton (1m, AW) on second run since being gelded and he followed up in fine style at Newbury (1m, good to firm); up 9lb since last time but this progressive 4yo could still play a leading role.

Two wins on the two Newmarket courses this season (1m, good to firm/good), the latest coming last month when held up; only fifth to Asmen Warrior at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago but saw plenty of daylight in a prominent position and may not have been seen to best effect; this lightly raced 4yo remains one to be interested in.

8yo who hasn't been at the top of his game this season (twice here); however, he took a step back in the right direction when sixth of 13 to Asmen Warrior at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last time and he may be able to build on it back at a track where he had a good record last season.
Mixed form this season but kept on well for close fourth at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last Saturday; might not be far away back up to 1m.

Won at Hamilton (1m1f, good) in May on second start for yard and third past the post in the competitive John Smith's Cup at York on July 11 (10.2f, good to firm; demoted to fifth due to interference); only fourth of five at Hamilton (8.3f, good to firm) five days later but set a steady pace, which may not have suited; not ruled out each-way.

0-13 since winning in April 2024 on his second start and the drop back to 1m poses a question; only sixth of nine at Sandown three weeks ago but running well previously; might have an each-way chance if bouncing back.

Twice close up in big-field handicaps at York (1m1f/1m, good) last month before fading when upped to 10.2f there (good to firm) a fortnight ago, when he failed to settle; could be a contender back down in trip.

Scored with authority on his return in Pontefract novice (6f, good to soft) in April; never on the pace when well-beaten eighth of 14 in 6f handicap here 12 weeks later but it's possible he'll benefit from this step up to 7f and remains unexposed after four starts; going than firmer than good would be a first.

Sent off 5-4 when beating six rivals on his debut at Newcastle (6f) in December; hasn't advanced his form in two subsequent outings but it was a sound start to his handicap career when third of 14 in 6f course handicap (good) latterly; stuck on after getting outpaced in a style which suggests this extra 1f will suit; has to enter the reckoning.

Promising start to handicap career, chasing home Toastmaster at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) before finishing a couple of places ahead of that rival when third of 11 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm again) a fortnight ago; handily drawn and should go well again.

OwnerName: Mrs Tabor, Mrs Mv Magnier, Mrs Shanahan
Spotlight: Narrow winner of a Beverley maiden in April; matched that when fifth on her handicap debut at Thirsk (1m, good) but two lesser runs have followed; Mr Noble is the more obvious of the Karl Burke pair.

Bar a blip on AW in the spring (wore a first-time tongue tie which was quickly discarded) his profile is steadily progressive, edging out Alpha Capture (due to run here on Friday) in 7f Doncaster handicap (good to firm) 16 days ago; 4lb higher now back in a 3yo only race but he may have more to give.

Built upon the promise of her debut fourth at Newbury (7f, good) in April when winning maiden at Lingfield (7f, AW) in May; well beaten on soft ground at Salisbury next time but bounced back with a respectable sixth on Chester handicap debut four weeks ago; that was a 0-95 so this represents a slight drop in grade; remains lightly raced for a leading yard.

Ex Irish-trained gelding who improved to make a winning start for Roger Fell in 7f Catterick novice in May; shaped quite well in handicaps over this trip on next two starts but in trouble before stamina should have been an issue when stepped up to 1m here since.

Ended time for Jane Chapple-Hyam by making all in 7f Yarmouth handicap (good to firm) four weeks ago; changed hands for 30,000gns since; new stable, which continues in good form, also runs Toastmaster; drawn wider than ideal.

OwnerName: Follow The Majer Partners & S Herrington
Spotlight: Struck at the third time of asking for Micheal Herrington when seeing off Flight Control and 11 others in handicap at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; Flight Control finished a couple of places ahead of him at the Newmarket July meeting since but it was another sound effort from this son of Cotai Glory.
Of interest on her 2yo best but beaten a long way on both 6f starts this year; the combination of a step up in trip and addition of a tongue-tie needs to spark a big upturn in his fortunes.

Shaped well when runner-up on three successive starts (6f/7f, good to soft/soft) but never better than midfield when faced with a firmer surface over 1m here 15 days ago; quickly drops back in trip with a visor also added.
Got up late to win a 5f Catterick novice (good to firm) in May but beaten upwards of 10l in his five other starts, including course handicaps over 5f and 1m the last twice.

Didn't enjoy the smoothest of passages when beaten a short head on handicap debut at Southwell (7f, AW) in April; hung right in the closing stages when good third of ten at Musselburgh (1m, good) ten days later; absent 104 days since; retains unexposed potential after only five starts.

Beaten on first ten starts but got off the mark at the 11th attempt at Ripon (6f, good) in May and followed up in big field at Doncaster (7f, good); his winning run was ended back at Doncaster but ran with credit again in fourth.
Won a Carlisle nursery (6f, good) last August; best run since when fourth of 20 over C&D (good) but failed to build on it when fifth of nine at Catterick 17 days ago.

6-24 on AW but 0-13 on turf; returned to form when second over C&D (good; Class 3) two weeks ago but he dictated steady fractions from the front and it probably flatters him; still commands some attention.
Capable handicapper off this mark but has gone badly off the boil in last three races, admittedly in higher grades; still has a bit to prove now and failed to fire on his previous visit here.

Front-runner who went off too fast for his own good over the extended 7f here two weeks ago and folded, which was also the case in his two previous runs; on a handy mark if he did get any freedom up front, though stamina doubts remain over quite this far.
French turf/AW winner (7.5f/1m2f) early in 2023; choppy waters afterwards and has been absent since finishing tailed off in the Chester Plate in May 2024.
Two 1m4f wins for Ben Brookhouse last year; hasn't seriously threatened back on the Flat for current yard (best effort was here in May) and ideally wants further.

Winning miler for Andrew Balding; quiet stable debut but has perked up for blinkers, going close at Ayr (1m2f) and Hamilton (8.3f); kept on well last time, suggesting this return to further will benefit.

Kingman filly who is a half-sister to the high-class Barney Roy; after two near misses (7f/8.6f) she got off the mark by a neck in a small-field 1m2f novice at Doncaster (good to firm); mixed messages as to the strength of that form but she brings potential into handicaps.
Best handicap display came at Down Royal in May when third over 7f; didn't reproduce that at Leopardstown 16 days ago, when tenth of 22 and 5.25l behind Yquem; likely capable of better.

Maiden produced back-to-back solid runs at Ballinrobe and the Curragh earlier this season; has failed to reach the same standard in last four starts; too keen when 13l behind the winner at Killarney (1m, good) latest.

Gained a fourth career win with a 22-1 success at Cork in May in testing conditions; not so good since on faster ground, finished in midfield at Killarney over an extended 1m3f last time; others more likely.

Made a flying start to his career with this yard when successful over 1m on stable debut on AW off 51 in January in a first-time hood; well below that level in two subsequent runs at Dundalk, and his two recent efforts over hurdles were not amazing either.

Doubled his tally and gained a first turf win when successful by a head over an extended 1m4f at Limerick two weeks ago (good); the top four finished in a heap that day so he's up just 1lb; drops back to his AW winning trip; thereabouts once again.

Took a big step forward from her stable debut when beating Nibras Rainbow by 3.5l at Leopardstown in June (1m1f, good to firm); ran to the same level in a similar contest last time when 1l third to Nibras Rainbow off 10lb higher; shortlisted.

1-43 on turf; struggled on the AW last winter; made an okay return to turf at Roscommon when fifth (7.5f, good) but was very poor next time over 1m here; bounced back with a good sixth at Leopardstown next time (1m1f, good); another poor run at Naas three days ago; hard to trust.
Easily won a Tipperary handicap off 51 last summer (7.5f, good); yet to make an impact in six outings this season.
Her win came in a 1m Salisbury handicap back in 2023; two runs for new yard were not too encouraging.
Positive fourth over 1m at Naas last time (good) when ahead of Morning Approach and Master Garvey; that came following a 275-day break, so she's entitled to improve.

OwnerName: Mrs Helen Butler & Mrs Bernadette Fahey & Seamus Fahey
Spotlight: Three-time turf winner from 33 starts but nothing since 2023; recent form not too encouraging, behind a couple of these in eighth at Leopardstown last time (1m1f, good); 4lb wrong.
Yet to place from 11 starts; okay sixths in her last two runs; more needed.

OwnerName: Patrick M O'Brien/Larry Murray/Richard W Walsh/Derek Cummins
Spotlight: 1-35 on turf; behind a couple of these when 11th of 18 at Naas (1m, good) last time; blinkers replace the previously-worn visor, but others more likely.
Course winner (6f/7f); not at her best in three runs this year but dropping down the weights and this is an ease in grade; has run well over C&D before but she may need more of a test.
The form of his 5f win at Wolverhampton in May has been franked since; a 5lb higher mark should be in range and the booking of Billy Loughnane suggests he will be ready to go after 81 days off.

Appeared to show improvement when fourth of eight at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago but they went steadily to halfway and it may not be a reliable piece of form; yard do well with this type though and she is at least unexposed.

Three-time AW winner, two of them over C&D, and he is 4lb lower than for his win here last September; wouldn't judge him too harshly on a couple of low-key 6f runs when last seen; strong claims back at 5f on AW.

Big prices and he has run to a modest level in three sprint novices this year; did hint at better last time and his trainer has enjoyed plenty of success with his half-brother Sugar Baby; worth a market check now handicapping.
11-race maiden; threatened on turf in the spring but his progress has stalled more recently; looks to have a bit to prove.
Course winner (6f) for another yard in February 2025; runner-up over C&D in June and a subsequent lesser effort on turf isn't the run to judge her on; each-way shout.
Exposed low-grade maiden; 80-1 when well held over 6f here four weeks ago.
Runner-up at Catterick (5f, good to soft) and Beverley (5f, good to firm) this summer; not so good at Southwell on Thursday but this test could suit better.
Seven-race maiden who was held at Carlisle (6f, soft) last month following a wind operation; others have stronger claims.

Hugely progressive as a 3yo, winning three times; highly tried this year and he has run with credit in defeat, notably his Listed third at Naas in April; 9lb higher than for his last handicap run (a 5f win at Doncaster) and could prove vulnerable.
Powered clear of his rivals in a 6f handicap at Windsor last month; reared at the start and missed the break over C&D a fortnight ago; perhaps a shade high in the weights for now.

Enjoyed his finest hour when winning the Palace Of Holyrood House Stakes at the Royal meeting in 2024; gained his first win since when narrowly landing a 5f handicap at Musselburgh in April; two solid efforts have followed and he would appear likely to make another bold bid.

Kept on well when winning a 6f handicap (good) here in May; not so good on his next two starts but he ran well for third back here (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; drops back to 5f with cheekpieces enlisted; others preferred for the win.

OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Xii & Mrs G Cowell
Spotlight: Patchy record for his new stable this year but he has run well over C&D in the past and has dropped to a tempting mark; cheekpieces replace blinkers today; couldn't discount.

Two C&D runs have seen him make the frame in big-field events; easily saw off four rivals in a handicap at Ffos Las (5f, good) 26 days ago; the combination of a 7lb rise and considerably more demanding opposition could scupper a follow up.

His two Ascot defeats came at the Royal meeting when a big outsider; arrives on the back of an easy win at Newmarket (5f, good to firm; visor reinstated) but a 6lb rise for that could leave him vulnerable.

Stays 6f well but he isn't short of speed and this belated first attempt at 5f looks an interesting move; arrives in top form, successful at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) 24 days ago, and a 4lb rise still leaves him with handicapping potential.

Snapped a losing sequence when down in class to score at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month; not so good under a penalty at Epsom 24 days ago; unplaced in all five visits to Ascot, albeit in stiff company.
Ex-Irish 4yo; slow start to life with this stable but he has dropped in the weights and his last two runs have been more encouraging, notably his Pontefract third eight days ago; should go well.

Ran a stormer over C&D on his seasonal return; the ground went against him at Epsom on Derby day and he has quickly bounced back with placed efforts at Beverley and Newmarket; up 2lb for latest near-miss but still on a good mark; Oisin Murphy booked; decent chance.

Won two of his five starts as a 2yo, including a wide-margin nursery success at Wolverhampton in November; he hasn't seen his race out in two handicap runs this year (5f/6f) but he should be sharper for last month's return from a break, he represents a yard that excels with this type and he has few miles on the clock; revival not out of the question.

Won at Royal Ascot in 2023 and second in this race in 2025; the handicapper has been in command for much of 2026 but he went close at Windsor last month; not in the same form at Newmarket two weeks ago but the switch from cheekpieces to a visor could help; contender.
Won twice at Ayr (6f) in novice/maiden company last term either side of a heavy defeat in the Coventry Stakes; has struggled so far this year, including when 100-1 for his stable debut 15 days ago.

Won four times over hurdles between July and September last year; lost his way in that sphere and struggled this summer in his first three Flat runs (1m2f-1m6f) but he should have a future in Flat handicaps, as he showed when winning well in a small field at Thirsk (1m4f, good to firm) on Friday; hard to beat under a penalty if in the same form.

Regressive 6yo who has struggled in five hurdle runs this year and was well held back on the Flat in a classified event here (1m4f, AW) 12 days ago; this step back up in trip should suit but losing run is up to 20 and all of his three wins have been on AW; others preferred.

Six-race maiden who has flopped at Wolverhampton (1m4f/1m6f) in his last two runs but he showed promise with his keeping-on third in a Ffos Las handicap (1m4f, good to soft) last month; that form puts him in the picture and he's a player if he can get back on track with blinkers added.

Inconsistent 15-race maiden but he was front-running third at Windsor (11.4f, good to firm) in May and it was the same story behind a handicap blot at Epsom (1m4f, good) last time; this is a new test at this trip but he has possibilities if his stamina holds out.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Can lack some concentration as when holding on last week at Doncaster (5f), for her second win in three starts; up 4lb and they claimed 5lb last week, so has more on her plate from stall 9.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
OwnerName: Ownaracehorse, O Pears and T&T Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Five-time turf winner but unraced here; had the cheekpieces back on when always close up to finish second at Beverley last time out; same mark and no excuses on the draw front.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Consistent 4yo who was close up in a higher grade at Sandown before another placed effort at Newbury; however, she's got the worst of the draw and is handicapped about right.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Better known for his AW exploits (7-26) and he's now 0-16 on turf after finishing last at Lingfield following 99 days off; hard to warm to from stall 11.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Rattled off a seven-timer on the AW earlier this year; rated lower on turf but went off 40-1 here recently on his return from a break and trailed in last.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Not hit top gear this year but signs of a return to form when keeping on from off the pace here 14 days ago in a race he won the previous year; always dangerous if getting a strong pace to chase.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: A winner for the Crisfords; nearly won again at Musselburgh in April (5f) but has trailed home last in his two races since, latterly with a tongue-tie and blinkers tried (now removed); drawn wide.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: 8lb lower than when beaten a head in a division of this last year; missed the kick here two weeks ago but nothing finished better and he looks ready to win again.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: 2-4 on the AW as opposed to 0-11 on grass; hasn't got a lot going since back from a break.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins over 6f but he's quick and well drawn for a front-runner; however, has been confined to the AW since contesting two turf maidens at the start of his career (one here); if handling the surface he might run well.

RaceName: Family Fun Day On 2nd August Handicap
Spotlight: Well drawn and was never far away when runner-up at Thirsk and Bath (both at 5f); lightly raced and may well improve some more; this will be a new experience but he enters the reckoning.

Useful 2yo in Britain (Listed 7f winner) and ran some fair races in the face of stiff tasks as a 3yo; returned from a 217-day absence at Lingfield on AW (7f, 15-8 fav) in February, having been gelded, but folded quickly; makes stable debut now, but needs to return to his best to win in a contest where others are treated slightly better by race conditions.

Ex-Ballydoyle; won Lingfield Derby Trial last year but well held in Irish Derby and Irish St Leger; bought for 78,000gns and has been soundly beaten in two hurdle races and a Curragh Listed contest for new yard; top rated of these, but others bring more compelling recent form.

Eight-race maiden has finished second in five of his races, including his last four; good effort in a four-runner C&D race on just his second turf run last time when 1.5l behind Trustyourinstinct, who has since won a Group 2; would receive 8lb from Summer Is Tomorrow in a handicap, so has work to do but he's consistent.

Nicely treated by race conditions and has run good races in second in his last two starts; beaten just a neck in a premier handicap at the Curragh in June (1m1f, good); failed to justify 11-10 favouritism at Navan last time when going down by a head; leading chance again.

Lightly-raced 4yo won a 7f AW maiden on debut in September 2024; well held in four runs last year in good-class company; always behind returned to Dundalk last time (1m4f); needs to bring more in first-time blinkers and treated poorly at weights.

OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: One of two for trainer; sole success came in a 3yo Dundalk maiden early last year; didn't run a bad race in a Curragh Listed contest in June when just 1.75l behind the winner (1m, good); out of her depth in a Curragh Group 3 last week; has the rating to be involved at this level.
Trailed home last at the Curragh on debut (6.5f, good to yielding); better on AW in cheekpieces next time when weakened into fifth of ten over 1m; others more likely.
By champion sire in South Africa, Vercingetorix; dam South African 5.5f-1m2f winner (inc 2yo/Grade 1; RPR 101); there are easier races in which to debut but worth a market check.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
OwnerName: The Jocks And The Geordies II
Spotlight: Has modest 1-31 strike-rate but gave good account when third of 13 in 6f handicap here last month and now dips into this basement grade for the first time; fine over 7f; high on the list.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Won two 7f Catterick handicaps in May and was placed in this grade at Wolverhampton (7f) when back on AW last month; didn't fire when back at Catterick 17 days ago but still a major player here.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Needs to bounce back quickly from duff effort on turf nine days ago but has been placed here three times (7f-1m) since his 1m course win in February and has a big role to play if back on song.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Brian Ellison Racing Club & M Dale
Spotlight: Versatile 7yo who gave fairly good account when fifth in 1m2f handicap here last month, after a 556-day absence; that run might have brought him on but this is his first 7f start since 2022.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Ursa Major & Mark Walford Racing Club
Spotlight: Held on gamely to make all in 1m handicap here last month and is now 2-31; evidently in good nick but this drop back in trip is not sure to suit.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-17 but bettered his low-key seasonal debut when second in this grade at Nottingham (6f, soft) last month and will also be suited by today's trip and ground combination; a possible.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Veteran who gained the last five of his 13 wins here (7f-1m); not firing on all cylinders in recent weeks, though, and needs to up his game.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Eight-race maiden; respectable fourth in Catterick handicap (good) when upped to 7f and fitted with cheekpieces in May but last month's 6f run was a backward step; cheekpieces now removed; tongue-tie added.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Always behind in 6f Redcar handicap last month and now 0-7; wore a visor last time; cheekpieces given a whirl here; considered only if lively in the betting.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Not beaten far when sixth of nine on handicap debut at Doncaster (7f, good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) in May but came last of ten on latest turf start; others have much stronger claims.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Displayed promise when fourth of six in Catterick novice (7f, good) in April and may not have handled soft ground when soundly beaten in her other two qualifying races; remains unexposed and is sure to appreciate this ease in grade on AW debut; interesting.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Seven-race maiden who has struggled to get competitive off basement marks in handicaps in recent months; swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Beaten about 8l when third in Redcar handicap (7f, good) last month but has now been placed on consecutive starts over that C&D; should be fine back on Tapeta; more appealing than most.

Added to his Ripon win last summer when justifying favouritism with a comfortable success at Ffos Las (1m2f, good; 2-1) last Monday; remains feasibly treated off only 3lb higher and he has form figures of 33511 at this trip; key player.

0-6 but he was runner-up in a handicap here (7.6f, good) in May and he made late gains when a close fifth at Windsor (1m, good to firm; cheekpieces added) last month; still has potential and he looks interesting on this step up to 1m2f.

Record of 2-38 but his last win was on AW here (1m2f) in March and he went close in an Epsom handicap (1m2f, good) three weeks ago; only 1lb higher than for that last run and he's respected on this drop back in grade.

Hasn't won since 2023 but he went close in a Brighton handicap (1m2f, good to firm) last month; has claims on that form but he's not easy to predict and was beaten 15l back at Brighton two weeks ago; risks attached.
Well held in all six runs including three handicaps (1m2f/1m) this summer; dropped another 2lb but she needs a transformation back up in trip.
Big prices and he's not finished closer than 13l to a winner in his five starts and has a best RPR of 35; opposable back in trip.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: James Dellaway And Jon & Kay Collins
Spotlight: Out of a 6f Listed 2yo winner who has produced a US Grade 3 winner; displayed only a modicum of promise when a down-the-field 33-1 shot on debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-brother to Irish 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Aloha Star; looked threatening before fading into fifth behind impressive winner at Newbury (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; should build on that performance here.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Starman (6f including Group 1 July Cup) and Sunday Star (Group-placed 6f/7f); good market support will bring her into the equation.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a useful and well-connected 6f 2yo winner; made promising debut at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago, keeping on well from the rear and losing out only by a neck, and makes obvious appeal.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ran well to finish fourth in useful seller at Chester (6f, good) in May, but that is her standout effort from six starts and she failed to beat a rival in a nursery at Catterick (cheekpieces added) last time; opposable.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 0-5 but she was placed on AW here (6f) last month and bounced back with a respectable fourth in a Bath maiden (5f, firm) last week; needs to find something extra but cheekpieces are now added and this step back in trip looks a good move.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 3,000gns yearling; 14-1 on C&D debut (good to firm) ten days ago and she never got involved before finishing a well-held fifth of seven; should know more this time but she needs plenty of improvement; hood removed.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 28-1 and she beat only one rival in a 13-runner maiden at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) last month.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Made a low-key start at Yarmouth in May but she's been placed in both subsequent runs, most recently when runner-up at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago; that form puts her in the picture and she should have more to offer; respected.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Never dangerous when 9-2 on recent Ripon debut (6f, good) but she made some late headway into fourth and that was a promising effort; should be more streetwise this time and she's a likely improver on her second start.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Didn't show much at Ascot (5f, good) in May but she returned after a break with a bold bid behind an odds-on rival at Epsom (7f, good to firm) two weeks ago; sets the standard on that form and she's open to more progress on this drop back in trip; big player.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 18,000euros yearling; fourth foal; half-sister to winners Calla Lagoon (Listed-placed 7f 2yo; RPR 101) and Calanthe (1m AW; 79); dam maiden (70) half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Calyx, out of 1m 2yo Group 3 winning sister to 6f Group 1 winner African Rose; yard 14% with 2yos this year and market should guide on debut.

RaceName: Pristine Homes Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Tailed off in her first two starts but she showed promise when a strong-finishing third at Bath (5f, firm; 80-1) last week; ties in with Last Dandelion on that form and she's open to more progress on this step back up in trip; not ruled out.

Raced too freely and was slightly disappointing when fifth in 1m2f Pontefract maiden this month but made the frame over that trip on first two starts and will be a threat if able to match that level of form over 1m.

Sixth foal; brother to 7f winner Consecrated (RPR 98), closely related to two winners including Enshrine (1m; 81), half-brother to 5f-7f winner Sacred (including Group 2; 116); dam French 12.5f winner, half-sister to US 1m-1m2f Grade 1 winner Lady Eli; with a top stable and no surprise if he features on debut; tongue-tie fitted.
Fair form when fourth on both starts, latterly in six-runner Redcar novice (1m2f, good) five weeks ago; needs to improve here but is well bred and has the potential.
Struggled when 250-1 for debut at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) 18 days ago.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: £130,000 half-brother to four juvenile winners; made a promising start when runner-up at Salisbury (5f, good) in May and his disappointing run at Wolverhampton (last of seven) was just four days later; been gelded since but he needs watching in the market back from a break.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 28-1 and he's finished down the field in 5f novice events at Windsor and Chepstow (both on good to firm); has plenty to find here and nurseries will be more suitable.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showcasing colt; third foal; dam 5f/6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 95), half-sister to winners Tone The Barone (prolific 5f/6f) and Mrs Gallagher (5f/5.5f Listed), out of Listed-placed 6f winner; plenty to like on paper and yard has 42% record with 2yos this season.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Disappointing at Newbury two weeks ago but that was an 18-runner novice and he showed good pace when third on his Windsor debut (6f, good to firm) last month; has possibilities if he can build on that and he has shaped as though this drop in trip could suit.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Made a solid start when second of five at Goodwood (5f, good) last month; never dangerous when highly tried in a Listed race at Sandown three weeks ago but he didn't get the best of runs and was only beaten 4l; sets a good standard back in calmer waters and he's a key player for in-form yard.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: E Kelly, J Woods, N Gallagher & Partner
Spotlight: Finished in rear in 6f novice events at Windsor and Newbury (both on good to firm), with a best RPR of 54; remains best watched for now.

RaceName: RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well held in all three runs, most recently when a 7l third of five at Bath (5f, good) last month; stablemate of It Dunt Marra and she can only be watched.

Came good for current stable at third attempt, with quite stylish success at Ripon (6f, good) last month; still on good mark after recent 4lb rise and this stiffer track ought to suit him; good chance.

Unexposed filly who made the frame in all three qualifying races, most recently when second in Chester maiden (7f, good) on seasonal/stable debut a fortnight ago; drops back in trip for handicap debut; probably still has potential.

Spoiled chance by refusing to settle on seasonal/stable but this month's midfield finish at Newbury (6f, good to firm) was more encouraging; has slipped to a dangerous mark and should now be approaching concert pitch.
Didn't find much after travelling strongly at Newbury (6f, good to firm) last month but that was his first run since February and he's on a good mark if the outing brought him on.
Dual C&D winner, more recently in this race a year ago (good to firm); has questions to answer after some below-par recent efforts but is too well handicapped to rule out.
Progressive mare who won twice over C&D this spring (good/soft) and led close home to complete her hat-trick at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; could still have more to offer; respected.

Returned from break with disappointing run in May but placed twice since, more recently when close second of five over C&D (good to firm) a fortnight ago; can go well from the front again but others appeal more.

Runner-up twice this spring (5.7f/5f) but form has dipped on last two outings; needs to be perked up by switch from usual cheekpieces to first-time blinkers, and to prove himself on fast ground (only win came on heavy).

A maiden after nine starts but all three runs this season have been respectable, and she appeared not to use her energy efficiently when a weakening sixth at Leicester (6f, good to firm) last time; hooded for first time here; enters calculations.
Displayed some promise in three 2yo maiden/novice races last summer (5.7f-6f) but this seasonal/stable/handicap debut comes after a one-year absence, and she's entitled to benefit from the outing.

Half-sister to five winners including Queues Likely (5f-1m including German Group 3; RPR 99); well held in her first two starts but her form really took off with a clearcut win in a C&D novice (good; 5-1) last month; looks on a fair mark now switched to handicap and she has plenty of scope for further progress; interesting contender.

Runner-up on AW here in her last two starts including a close call in a novice (5f) in December and a 3l second on handicap debut (6f) 12 days ago; should benefit from that last run and she's still unexposed after only four starts; in the mix back on turf.

Won a Ripon maiden (5f, good) last June; highly tried in Listed events in final two juvenile runs but she's not threatened in five handicaps for new yard this season; mark continues to fall but she struggled at Nottingham last time and others are preferred.

Off the mark at the eighth attempt with a narrow win at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) last month; couldn't pose a serious threat when third at Leicester last time but she finished well and that was an eye-catching effort; still unexposed as a sprint handicapper and has claims if she gets a good pace to aim at.

Plenty of near-misses before finally off the mark over 5f at Bath (good) last month; still looks on a workable mark but she's not easy to predict and was disappointing after a slow start at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) last time; risks attached.

Resurgent 4yo who won an apprentice handicap at Salisbury (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces added) two weeks ago and she didn't get much luck when a close second at Chepstow last Wednesday; 2lb higher here but she remains well treated on old form and is strongly respected.

Three sprint wins on turf and her last success was off 10lb higher at York last June; has been up and down for new yard this season but she was placed at Newbury (6f, good to firm) last time and has claims if she can back that up.

Scored over 1m on Polytrack in May and placed twice behind same progressive rival over that trip on turf at Ffos Las last month; benefits from Mason Paetel's useful 5lb claim here and shapes as though well worth a crack at 1m2f; might be the answer.

Posted career-best performance when winning on Poytrack at Lingfield (1m2f) in April, after a break, but subsequent turf form has been underwhelming and he's still on a fairly tough mark; cheekpieces refitted in bid to perk him up.

Easily won three-runner juvenile hurdle last month but reverts to the Flat after odds-on defeat six days later; will be suited by the trip/ground here and is probably on a workable mark but a couple of the others have less to prove; sports first-time cheekpieces.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Battled well to prevail in bunch finish at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm) this month, opening account at fifth attempt; only 2lb higher and still unexposed over this trip; ought to make her presence felt again.

100,000gns foal; well held in his first two starts but he really got his act together with a comfortable win in a Brighton (6f, good to firm) last month; opening mark is no gift but he has a useful pedigree and could have a lot more to offer in handicaps; key player.

Justified favouritism in a Goodwood novice (6f, good) last May but he's 0-8 since and has been inconsistent; now 7lb lower than for his opening mark but he struggled at Epsom last time and others are more convincing; tongue-tie added.

Two sprint wins in Ireland as 2yo, including when making all at the Curragh (6f, good) last August; well handicapped on that form but he's struggled since and has form figures of 89089 for his current yard; lost to prove.

Has a patchy profile but she won over C&D (good) in May and got back on the scoresheet with a narrow success at Yarmouth (5f, good to firm) ten days ago; up 3lb but she was as good as ever last time and she's respected back at this track.

Made the breakthrough at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in May and he's finished a creditable third on turf (1m, good to firm) and Tapeta (7f) since; now returns to sprinting but he has plenty of form at this trip and still looks on a workable mark; in the mix.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Suited by step up in trip when keeping on well for clearcut success at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) last week ago and now 2-7; open to further progress over this distance; likely contender.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field on first two starts (1m/1m2f) but fared better when third of seven here (1m2f, good to firm) last month, albeit no threat to front pair; should have more improvement to come in handicaps.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
Spotlight: Denied clear run before keeping on well to go close on handicap debut at Newbury (1m2f, good) in May and, after struggling on soft ground, again ran well when fourth over that C&D (good to firm) three weeks ago; upped in trip here; must be considered.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
OwnerName: P Hickman And Lord Lloyd Webber
Spotlight: May have been flattered by proximity when third of six in steadily run Redcar novice (1m2f, good) last month and has since finished last in a Yarmouth maiden over that trip; however, this well-bred gelding is open to improvement in handicaps.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
OwnerName: J O'Mulloy And W R Muir
Spotlight: Runner-up on two of his three starts this season, losing out by only a neck after game attempt to make all at Chepstow (1m4f, good to firm) this month; moves up from 0-60 grade today, though.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed after only four runs but was just a respectable fourth of six in 0-55 grade on last month's handicap debut at Chepstow (1m2f, good to firm) and is effectively 1lb higher from out of the weights here; needs combination of new trip and first-time cheekpieces needs to prompt improvement.

Record of 1-20 on turf but that win was off 1lb lower at Goodwood in May; hasn't matched that form in three subsequent runs but he ran into a well-handicapped rival when a 4l second at Salisbury (5f, good to firm) last time; now drops back into a Class 5 event and he's not ruled out.

Won a Leicester maiden (5f, good) on stable debut last July but he struggled in handicaps in his final two runs last season; overall record is now 1-10 and he has something to prove after 277 days off.

Four-time AW winner who is 0-11 on turf but finished well to snatch second in a C&D handicap (good to firm) last month; left Richard Hughes for 15,000gns since; on same mark as last time and he's a player if he gets a good pace and some luck; cheekpieces are removed.

Front-runner who won over C&D last summer and was a creditable second in a Class 4 at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) last week; hasn't had much luck with the draw but he's 1lb lower than last time and is a big player if he can repeat that form.
Six-time winner, with five on AW and one on turf; well handicapped on his Nottingham win (5f, good) last summer but he's been out sorts in three runs this season and needs a big turnaround.

Just 1-16 but his win was over C&D (good) last summer; has been up and down this season but he had a near-miss at Goodwood in May and was a fair third on AW here last time; usually races prominently and it wouldn't be a surprise if he made a bold bid.

Unexposed 3yo who returned after a year off with a promising second in a Nottingham novice (5f, good to firm; first run after wind surgery) three weeks ago; flashed her tail in that race but it's still early days and she needs a close look on handicap debut.
Nine-race maiden who is yet to hit top gear after three runs in blinkers this season (1m-1m2f); slipping down the weights but needs to up her game; refitted hood is added to the blinkers.
Came good with two narrow wins last month in Chepstow handicap (1m, good) and Lingfield classified (7.6f, good to firm); may need to find a bit extra but is respected in her current mood.
0-15 under all codes and absent since well-held fourth over hurdles in October; will probably find this trip too sharp; best to look elsewhere.

2-2 since switched to handicaps this season, with both wins gained over 7f on fast ground; raised just 1lb for latter success and the form has been well advertised by the runner-up since; hard to beat if stamina holds out over this new trip.
Dangerously handicapped on old form but looked out of sorts during five-race turf/AW spell from August to January; gelded in March; needs to have been revitalised by 203-day break.

Began season with three disappointing runs but was seeemingly aided by first-time blinkers (retained) when third at Leicester (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago, when she was denied a clear run close home and might have been unlucky; another 1lb lower for first attempt at 1m; one to consider.

Spotlight: On target four times in her last seven outings; scored in the Acorn Stakes last month; jockey's C&D record from low draws is useful and expected to be in the thick of things.
Missed the frame (beaten 7l into sixth) in an allowance Grade 3 at Churchill Downs two months ago; on target twice in her last five outings.
Bids to pull off a hat-trick; won a black type by just over 2l at Churchill Downs last month; this is the only ride on the card for Axel Concepcion; easy enough to take on despite that win last time

OwnerName: Trott Racing Stable, Five Sisters Farm & John Polizos
Spotlight: Career wins-runs record of 4-11; 15-2 winner by just over 2l at Delaware Park last month in a black type; despite that Delaware Park success, unlikely to trouble the principals; also engaged in race 7 at Monmouth Park.

OwnerName: Gary Barber, Bridlewood Farm & Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners
Spotlight: Went down by 1l behind Directive last month in an allowance optional claimer.

OwnerName: Douglas Scharbauer & Three Chimneys Farm LLC
Spotlight: Behind Counting Stars when beaten just under 4l to finish second in the Acorn Stakes last month; has won three of her four career runs and landed the Kentucky Oaks three months ago; major player.
Landed a narrow success in an allowance optional claimer last month; aiming to complete a hat-trick and has made an impressive start to her career with two wins from three starts; in the mix.

Behind Always A Runner at Churchill Downs when sixth of 13 in the Kentucky Oaks in May; winner of three of her five runs to date; wears first-time blinkers; warrants consideration as has some big wins on the CV; also engaged in race 7 at Monmouth Park.

No impression when fourth of eight in April, finishing well behind reopposing Always A Runner at Aqueduct in an allowance Grade 3; workout history raises concerns this race may be needed so not hard to turn elsewhere; was due to run at Saratoga Friday.
